chapters.title: Chapter 151 It happened suddenly
paragraphs: The next day, Zhang Yulan came again.
She was getting a little addicted, almost to the taste.
And coincidentally, Wu Yangjun also arrived, having just left the palace, wanting to find a big cock to fuck her.

The two were old acquaintances. Zhang Yulan, as a physician, had been summoned to Changqiu Palace to treat the Empress and Wu Yangjun. Female physicians treating women were only practiced in the palace; other powerful families wouldn’t train such doctors, as it was unnecessary.
Lu Ming had just finished with Zhang Yulan when Wu Yangjun arrived. Luckily, he had just finished, otherwise they would have had to fuck each other together.
At this moment, the steward, Wu Ben, rushed over and whispered in his ear, "Master, He Xian is here again!"

"Hmm, I know. You may leave now." Lu Ming nodded, dismissed Wu Ben, and then bowed to Wu Yangjun, saying, "Madam, He Xian is causing trouble at my shop. I’ll go deal with him first. Please wait here for a moment, Madam."
Wu Yangjun was displeased upon hearing this, not with Lu Ming, but with He Xian!
In fact, Wu Yangjun was not He Jin’s mother, but his stepmother, meaning she had no real connection to He Xian and He Jin’s son.
However, she was still an elder, especially when she wanted to find a big penis to fuck, and her grandson was causing trouble. Naturally, she was unhappy.
"Please wait, my lord. I’ll go with you. That brat He Xian is outrageous! I think the General’s lack of discipline is the reason he’s making such a fool of himself."

"Very well, unless absolutely necessary, Madam need not intervene. I will handle my affairs. No one can subdue me, not even the General." Lu Ming’s tone was filled with confidence and pride. His masculine charm made Zhang Yulan and Wu Yangjun somewhat aroused. Once Lu Ming had slept with them, it was hard to forget the pleasure he brought.
The body is conquered, can the soul be far behind?
South of the city market, Lu’s Barbecue Restaurant.

A large crowd was watching from a distance. An arrogant young man sat on the back of a shopkeeper, pinning him to the ground, his expression extremely arrogant. "Selling such inferior ingredients, if I get sick from eating them, what will you do?"
"My lord, I’m innocent! I personally tasted everything, there’s nothing wrong with it." The shopkeeper, bruised and battered, still insisted there was nothing wrong.
Because there was truly no problem, he dared not admit to any; admitting it would only lead to more serious consequences.
If he admitted it, the owner of the shop would also suffer. These privileged sons of nobles loved to escalate things.
"Still dare to argue! Beat them! Kill these shady merchants!" He Xian grinned maliciously, ordering his men to smash and destroy. His father had been wronged; now his son would avenge him.
Outside, a crowd watched the spectacle, even from a distant tavern.
A handsome, well-built man watched the spectacle.
Accompanied by several strategists and generals, upon closer inspection, it was none other than Yuan Shao, the young and talented member of the Yuan family.
"Such a petty trick will likely fail, but it’s enough to annoy them," Yuan Shao said smugly. He didn’t need to intervene directly.
He only needed to announce at some point that the Grand General’s trusted minister had been murdered; the rest of the Yuan family members would be incited by He Xian.
The Yuan family possessed a vast collection of classical texts; anyone wishing to study had to align themselves with them.
Knowledge is power. Whether it was the Yuan, Yang, Wang, or any other aristocratic family, each possessed its own unique collection of books.
Studying was essential for becoming an official, and these families could decide who could receive an education.
He Jin also knew that studying could change his fate, but obtaining an education was incredibly difficult.
The best way was to go to the Yingchuan Academy, where he could study.
However, it was highly exclusive. There was also an academy in Yecheng, Hebei, which was similarly exclusive.

Local factions had always existed. Even under Dong Zhuo, there was constant infighting among small groups. Xu Rong, being from Liaodong, was directly excluded from the circle and forced to align himself with Lu Ming.
Now, to secure a future for his son, education was the only option.
Otherwise, when Emperor Ling died and the next emperor ascended the throne, he wouldn’t be the emperor’s brother-in-law anymore, and this great general would likely have to retire to his hometown!

At that time, all the glory and wealth would be gone. Therefore, to prepare for the future, and with the Yuan family’s influence, He Xian was sent to study at the Yuan family’s academy, thus binding him to their cause—a desperate measure.
Once bound, his actions would be out of his control.
Under the unspoken influence, or perhaps constantly hearing discussions about these matters, and being young, He Xian was easily swayed into causing trouble for Lu Ming.
This way, He Xian could be used as a shield while simultaneously venting Yuan Wei’s anger—a win-win situation!

"Lu Ming is young and belligerent. Facing the Grand General, he’s unlikely to have a good end. My lord, watching from the sidelines is a brilliant plan!" said a round-faced strategist, clearly a sycophant.

"Look, gentlemen, drink this cup to the brim! I’ve received word that Lu Ming is on his way." Yuan Shao’s tone was quite smug. He certainly wouldn’t lead the charge himself, but he had plenty of courage to act alongside Nie Chuan and the others.

As the crowd parted, Lu Ming arrived at the scene. He saw the barbecue grill overturned, the tables and chairs smashed, and even the shop itself vandalized. Sauces were scattered everywhere—it was clearly a demolition operation!

"He Xian, I have no past grudges or recent conflicts with you. Why are you pressuring me like this? Do you think you’re so great just because your father is a great general? Don’t think you can act recklessly just because the Yuan family is your dog!" Lu Ming snorted, walking over to see the other man pinning down his shopkeeper. "Get up first, apologize, and I’ll forgive you."

"Hahaha! What a joke! Who do you think you are! Just a dog, daring to talk to me? What right do you have!" He Xian had just finished speaking, smugly looking down at Lu Ming, not even bothering to glance at him.
*Slap! Thud!* A slap sent He Xian flying, followed by the sound of him crashing straight into the wall.

"He Xian has committed insubordination, attacked officers, and is plotting a rebellion! Arrest and bring all those involved into custody. Report this to the Court of Justice!" Lu Ming first beat up the arrogant and unruly young master, then preemptively tied him up.
Let’s get this straight first; we can deal with the rest later.
Everyone was stunned. This is outrageous! Plotting a rebellion? And he’s the son of a high-ranking general?

chapters.title: Chapter 152 Strike first
paragraphs: Swift and decisive, from his entrance to his departure, less than five minutes had passed; He Xian had been knocked unconscious and taken away.
His servants and three members of the Yuan family, along with He Xian, were also tied up, their mouths stuffed with smelly socks to silence them, and they were simply escorted away.
This scene left Yuan Shao, who had been watching from afar, completely bewildered. This was utterly unreasonable, relying solely on force!

"Outrageous! Allow me to return and report to my uncle; the Yuan family members must not be bullied!" Yuan Shao was thinking of consulting his uncle, Yuan Kui, for a solution, not personally protecting the Yuan family members he had banished.
To put it bluntly, the Yuan family was vast and powerful, with many collateral branches declining each year, numbering in the thousands, but their fates were generally ignored.
However, opportunities for education were still provided, with selection based on merit; those with ability were given a better life.
Those Yuan family members without ability were left to fend for themselves, some reduced to manual labor at the docks, others to prostitution.
Such behavior hardly befits a wise ruler. A ruler without responsibility, no matter how many talented individuals he has, is useless.
This scene had initially attracted much attention, but Lu Ming’s actions undoubtedly ignited the conflict!
The other side’s meddling was like flies, but Lu Ming’s accusation of rebellion was an act worthy of annihilation!
Even Lady Wuyang was startled, still pondering what to do.
Zhang Yulan, meanwhile, found an excuse to leave and consult with Princess Wannian.
Offending the Grand General might not end well.
Back at his residence, Lu Ming knew time was of the essence; he had to first go to the palace to meet the Emperor and explain the situation.
So he pulled Lady Wuyang aside, gave her some instructions, and then...had sex with her!
Because he was in a hurry, Lu Ming didn’t hold back. In just ten minutes, after a whirlwind of attacks, he ejaculated all his semen into Wu Yangjun’s cunt.
Wu Yangjun’s eyes rolled back in her head. Such intense thrusting almost killed her!
It was pleasurable, truly pleasurable, but her cunt suffered a bit. She’d probably have to be careful when urinating for the next few days, otherwise, the sharp pain would be quite unpleasant!
Just as he reached the door, he saw the eunuch Zhao Zhong approaching in person.
"Lord Zhao, what brings you here?" Lu Ming stepped forward, cupped his hands, and subtly handed over a jade pendant.
Zhao Zhong weighed the jade pendant in his hand, then quickly put it away. "By His Majesty’s decree, Commandant Lu is summoned to the palace for an audience."

He then added in a low voice, "Commander Lu, remnants of the Yellow Turban Rebellion are causing trouble in Hanoi. Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Yan and the Grand General have both recommended that you go to join the rebellion. His Majesty also intends for you to go. This trip to the palace is not of great importance."
"Thank you, Lord Zhao. I will surely repay you handsomely in the future!" Lu Ming replied with a cupped-hand salute, his expression somewhat serious. He was actually being sent to war?

Several groups of men split into several groups to act. Yuan Shao returned to the Yuan family to seek countermeasures, Zhang Yulan went to persuade Princess Wannian to intercede for Lu Ming, and Lord Wuyang returned to Changqiu Palace to plead with Empress He.

The key lies with Emperor Ling’s will, and Empress He’s influence is limited. However, He Jin dares not offend her. Firstly, she is the Empress; secondly, even if his eldest son Liu Bian ascends the throne, Empress He will become Empress Dowager, her power increasing rather than declining. Compared to her, He Jin still needs to rely on her.
In the Deyang Palace, Emperor Ling and General He Jin were already present.
Lu Ming arrived and glanced at He Jin, a bearded butcher, as fat as a ball. "Your Majesty, this humble subject greets you."

"Hmm, Anmin, no need for formalities. An urgent report has arrived from Hedong Commandery: Yellow Turban remnants have gathered 100,000 men to attack the commandery city. Prefect Fan Yi has requested reinforcements from the court. Now, both the Grand Master of Ceremonies and the General-in-Chief recommend you. What do you think?" Emperor Ling’s words were brief. Hedong was the gateway to Luoyang; the Yellow Turban remnants had already reached his doorstep, forcing him to take the matter seriously.
In reality, while the core areas of the Central Plains were relatively safe, remote regions were constantly attacked by bandits. Once breached, the city was utterly destroyed.
They dared not occupy cities, fearing annihilation by government troops, leaving only utter looting and devastation.
This severely weakened the population. Even if the region was conquered, insufficient manpower would lead to a lack of sustainability, making even production impossible.
The decline of the Han Dynasty was not a sudden event, but a gradual accumulation.

After considering his options, Lu Ming clasped his hands and said, "Your Majesty, I am willing to lead the army, but there is something I must report to Your Majesty, otherwise my heart will be uneasy. I do not wish to see those fighting valiantly on the front lines, shedding blood to protect the Han Dynasty, while shameless villains slaughter my family and devour my property."
These words were quite serious, clearly implying that someone was plotting behind the scenes. Who was this person?
Emperor Ling’s first suspicion fell on the Yuan family. Only the Yuan family had a deep-seated grudge against Lu Ming, and there was a reason for making an example of them.

"Speak freely, I will stand up for you!" Emperor Ling knew he had to make a show of force; otherwise, if the person he valued was targeted by the Yuan family, then imperial power would wane, and the emperor would become a puppet!
He absolutely would not allow this to happen!
In the past, he had acted recklessly, abandoning all shame for money.
But now, he needed to pave the way for his successor, and all obstacles must be removed!

"For five consecutive days, He Xian, the son of the Grand General, vandalized my shop without cause. These were gifts from His Majesty, and I had no choice but to protect them. However, He Xian repeatedly pressured me, leaving me with no way to retreat. He Xian claimed that Luoyang belonged to his He family and boasted that the He family army was invincible, threatening to kill my entire family. I had no choice but to retaliate, and now He Xian has been captured. I am willing to follow His Majesty’s lead, even at the cost of my life! But I cannot tolerate such despicable behavior from such a villain!"
Upon hearing this, He Jin felt a chill run down his spine!
Especially when Emperor Ling looked at him, he could feel a rage that had been suppressed to the extreme!
No one wanted, no, no emperor could allow such a thing to happen.
The He family army!
What immense power!
The Han army, under the control of a private individual—was this still the Han army?
"Your Majesty, I have failed in my duty to raise my son! I am guilty!" He Jin immediately knelt down, admitting his mistake and blaming it on his poor upbringing.
Making a big issue into a small one, and a small one into nothing, was his usual practice.
At the same time, he harbored extreme hatred for Lu Ming, and also felt a certain fear. The other party was truly despicable, aiming to kill without hesitation!

chapters.title: Chapter 153 Yang’s assistance
paragraphs: Emperor Ling was somewhat surprised, so he summoned Zhang Rang for questioning.
Although Zhang Rang didn’t know the specifics of the matter, he had heard some rumors.
Furthermore, his adopted son was gradually recovering thanks to Lu Ming’s treatment, and he didn’t want Lu Ming to take any risks.
If he died in battle, wouldn’t his adopted son also die?
And he hadn’t even had a grandson yet, so he couldn’t let Lu Ming die.

So, he exaggerated and spoke ill of He Xian, while subtly suggesting that Emperor Ling’s health still required Lu Ming’s treatment and that it was inconvenient for him to go to Hedong to quell the rebellion.
This made Emperor Ling conflicted again.
He wasn’t a particularly decisive person, especially when his own interests were involved; he was caught in a dilemma.

He didn’t have to believe everything Zhang Rang said, but he knew Zhang Rang wouldn’t harm him. It wasn’t because Zhang Rang was a servant, or because he often called him "Father Rang," but because these eunuchs would be utterly useless without him!
"In that case, Lu Ming still has to go, just for training. He can return no matter what. Summon Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun to the palace; I have something to say to them."
Emperor Ling, after much deliberation, could only bring out some veteran officials.
These were all capable military officers, who didn’t get involved in other matters. Even during the fiercest power struggles, they remained uninvolved and didn’t care if they were falsely accused.
They were very useful and extremely loyal tools.

"This matter will be handled by the Court of Justice. The truth must be thoroughly investigated. General, you will compensate Commandant Lu for all his losses. Any objections?" Emperor Ling quickly made his decision. "From now on, you are not allowed to seek revenge. You are all my trusted ministers; you must not attack each other!"
"Your subject obeys." The General was seething with hatred, but had no choice but to agree. His true intention was to eliminate Lu Ming the moment he lost his usefulness!

Lu Ming was also somewhat dissatisfied. This result was practically meaningless to He Jin, but he understood; after all, he was He Jin’s brother-in-law, and dealing with him was difficult. "Your subject obeys the decree."

"General, my loss is five thousand taels of silver. This must be a drop in the ocean for you, General. Since His Majesty has spoken, please deliver the money to my residence in the next couple of days. You are a wealthy and powerful man; surely you wouldn’t be a deadbeat and refuse to pay. If you can’t pay with cash, then collateral is acceptable, but it will be calculated at half the market value." Lu Ming was starting to make exorbitant demands. Five thousand taels was indeed not much for He Jin; it was only three months’ income, and he would only feel a slight pang of pain.

"You!" He Jin was furious. This was a blatant robbery! But with Emperor Ling as his guarantor, he knew it wasn’t just five thousand taels. If he didn’t want to pay, the consequences would be far more than five thousand taels. "I will send someone to deliver the money tomorrow, not a penny less!"
"That’s for the best. Thank you, General." Lu Ming knew he had offended another person.
Good heavens, Yuan Wei and He Jin, both powerful figures in the court, had been completely offended by him. There was no way out.
If he didn’t take a firm stance, he would be the one who got hurt. The other party would become even more arrogant, and then things would get very bad; the outcome would be dire!
To win, he had to go all out, fight to the death. Only through repeated desperate struggles could he force the enemy to retreat and concede benefits.

Emperor Ling and the generals, including Zhu Jun, discussed the matter for a long time before finally deciding to appoint Huangfu Song as commander, leading the Eight Colonels of the Western Garden to support Hedong.

chapters.title: Chapter 156 Captain Feng Fang, who bullies the weak and fears the strong
paragraphs: Before the army moves, supplies must be ready.
A steady stream of provisions was being gathered from various regions, and the troops from the Western Garden began to assemble and select their soldiers.
Lu Ming didn’t go. Emperor Ling had ordered him to form his own army, operating independently, which would inevitably lead to isolation.
He had to handle the provisions and supplies himself; there was no other way.
Of course, he could ask Huangfu Song for them. Although this stubborn old man disliked such things, he dared not disobey the emperor’s orders.
However, how his subordinates would make things difficult was unknown.
It was best to prepare for both possibilities and not rely too much on these people; testing the waters was always a good idea.
Unexpectedly, someone invited Lu Ming to his residence. It wasn’t Yuan Shu, the then-Minister of Justice, nor Princess Wannian, but Feng Fang, the Right Colonel of the Army!
Previously, Lu Ming had intervened when Feng Fang’s daughter, Feng Qin, was harassed by Wu Kuang’s son at the market, and many days had passed without a word from him.
Now, he was unexpectedly invited to his residence; this was quite strange.

Originally, Lu Ming hadn’t intended to pay any attention to such a person, but after seeing Feng Qin’s beauty, and considering she was historically Yuan Shu’s wife, his collecting obsession kicked in, and he naturally thought about how to get his hands on her.
The worse Feng Fang’s performance, the less Lu Ming would take him seriously in the future. What ability could someone who couldn’t even protect his family have?
Upon arriving at Feng Fang’s residence, he was refused entry by the servants and told to wait outside.
Lu Ming narrowed his eyes, sensing something was amiss.
He stroked his chin; he needed to analyze the situation.
Feng Fang had invited him to a banquet, but this servant had stopped him at the door.
So now there seem to be two possibilities. The first is unlikely; the servant acted on his own initiative and stopped him.
The second is that this banquet is probably a trap!
After waiting for a while, Feng Fang still hadn’t come out. Suddenly, Lu Ming threw a punch, sending the gatekeeper flying. He grabbed the man and strode forward.
*Swoosh!* The guards immediately drew their swords, their expressions as if facing a formidable enemy. "Sir, don’t go any further, or we’ll have to take action! Let him go!"
A sinister smile played on Lu Ming’s lips. He put the servant down, and just as the guards breathed a sigh of relief, he suddenly raised his foot and stomped down hard!
*Crack!* The sound of breaking leg bones rang out.
"Ah!"
The gatekeeper’s scream followed. Lu Ming stomped on him twice more, crippling both his legs.
With a sinister grin, he said, "Since Captain Feng repays kindness with enmity, so be it. We’ll see what happens next!"
"Wait!" Just as Lu Ming was about to leave, Feng Fang appeared.
He was dressed in plain clothes, a long sword hanging at his waist.
Seeing his servant slumped on the ground, screaming in agony, he frowned slightly.
"Captain Lu, what happened?"

"This servant not only refused to let me in when I presented the invitation, but also spoke arrogantly to me. Captain Feng, you invited me to a banquet. I waited outside for almost half an hour, and this is your way of treating guests?" Lu Ming’s tone was very unfriendly. His time was precious, and to waste it like this, he was already being very polite by not killing Feng Fang.
Feng Fang frowned slightly. He had genuinely been delayed and only wanted Lu Ming to wait.

But the servant had made Lu Ming wait at the gate without even inviting him in, which had caused a misunderstanding! "It was a mistake, but Lu Ming’s ruthless and direct crippling of the man was simply too much!"

"Captain Lu, I admit this was due to the servants’ negligence. I originally intended to have someone invite you inside to rest, but the servants made our honored guest wait outside. However, Captain Lu’s ruthless actions show a complete disregard for me, Feng!"

"Oh? You think you’re so great, so high and mighty! Where were you when your family was being bullied? Hmph, what a fine way to bully the weak with a gun, Feng Fang, you’ve really got it. Hmph, farewell!" Lu Ming finally saw through him; this was a complete idiot!
Yes, a complete idiot!
Invited me here, and didn’t even show proper courtesy. After this happened, instead of apologizing, he’s demanding an explanation?
What a joke!
Afraid to offend Wu Kuang, yet dares to talk back, huh!
"Lu Ming! Don’t push your luck!" Feng Fang felt his face burning with embarrassment. They were both captains, what was with the airs!
He genuinely didn’t dare offend General He Jin. He had originally invited Lu Ming to express his gratitude.
In fact, if his daughter had been insulted, he could use the marriage alliance with Wu Kuang to ride on the General’s coattails.
But things had been messed up!
If it weren’t for face and social etiquette, he wouldn’t have wanted to speak to Lu Ming at all!
What a waste of time!
Mind your own business!
Otherwise, he wouldn’t have waited so many days to belatedly invite him to the banquet.
This was already impolite, and now the conflict had escalated because of his own actions and the servant’s behavior.
If it weren’t for Lu Ming’s strength, Feng Fang would have already sent someone to capture him!
Their main tactic was to bully the weak and fear the strong, never daring to confront anyone head-on. Now that Lu Ming had shown some backbone, Feng Fang immediately backed down.
Having seen through Feng Fang’s intentions, Lu Ming, on the other hand, didn’t want to leave.
So, grinning maliciously, he said, "Looks like you don’t want me to leave! Fine, then let’s make a scene! Let’s go and reason with His Majesty! Draw your sword and kill all the guards!"
Lu Ming drew his longsword and charged forward.
Before Feng Fang could react, he kicked him away, then swept his sword horizontally, decapitating a guard!
The head flew high, a terrified expression still etched on the face!
Thud!
The longsword was as fast as lightning; wherever the blade touched, blood flowed instantly.

A feint thrust tricked another guard into raising his sword to parry, but the next second, Lu Ming changed his move, gripping the sword and slicing down, instantly cleaving the guard’s stomach open! His intestines spilled out, and with a backhand sweep, he chopped off his head again!

"Using a banquet as a pretext to ambush and assassinate a general about to lead his troops to quell the rebellion! You’ve got some nerve, Feng Fang! You must be a Yellow Turban remnant! Prepare to die!" Lu Ming immediately pinned the blame on Feng Fang!

He absolutely couldn’t tolerate someone who dared to use a banquet to trick him. He had to establish the impression and reputation of a madman, letting the Yuan family and He Jin know that offending him would mean facing the consequences of having pieces of their flesh torn off!

chapters.title: Chapter 157 Feng Fang, timid and cowardly
paragraphs: He had long heard of Lu Ming’s extraordinary skills, but seeing him today, he was practically a god of death reincarnated!
He wouldn’t dare claim to be the best in the world, but at least in Luoyang, there were few who could rival him.
Watching Lu Ming slaughter his way through, wiping out his guards in no time,
Feng Fang felt fear for the first time. He regretted his actions; had he been blinded by greed, thinking of targeting Lu Ming?
Such a man would eventually shine—no, he would rise to prominence!
Why had he treated him with prejudice just because he came from a humble background?
Lu Ming grinned maliciously, pulling him up and dragging Feng Fang along. "Come on, let’s go to the Court of Justice! I want to see what you’re up to, plotting to murder a high-ranking official!"
"Misunderstanding! Misunderstanding!" Feng Fang was terrified. He, Feng Fang, was the son-in-law of the eunuch Cao Jie.

Cao Jie was a powerful eunuch who had previously held immense influence at court. He had rendered meritorious service in welcoming Emperor Ling to the throne, and even the Ten Attendants had to avoid his advances.
Cao Jie was also shrewd; he avoided offending Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong, but he was less courteous to others.
He was essentially the one who framed and led the murders of Emperor Heng’s mother and her relatives.
If Cao Jie were still alive, Feng Fang would have enjoyed immense prestige.
However, his good fortune was short-lived. A few years ago, Cao Jie died, which triggered a purge.

First to be targeted was Cao Jie’s younger brother, Cao Poshi. When Cao Poshi served as the Commandant of the Yueqi Cavalry, a squad leader in the Yueqi camp had a beautiful wife, and Cao Poshi demanded her from the squad leader.
The squad leader dared not disobey, but the wife resolutely refused and committed suicide.
The Cao family was generally known for its debauchery and tyranny.
With so many people offended, the reckoning was inevitable.
Cao Jie’s adopted son and grandson both died tragically, their bodies left unburied and abandoned to be devoured by wild dogs.
And from the elderly to children, no one escaped!
This is the consequence of tyrannical taxation!
Retribution may be delayed, but it will surely come!

If Feng Fang hadn’t been timid and cautious, and hadn’t been favored by Emperor Ling as a henchman, he too would likely have suffered the same fate—family ruin, corpses lying in the streets, without a proper burial!
This is why he remained somewhat indifferent even when his daughter was nearly violated.
He simply didn’t want trouble, and even wished his daughter hadn’t caused him any trouble!
All these years, he’d kept a low profile, just to survive.
Now, even without offending the General or the Yuan family, trouble still found him!

"My lord, my lord, let’s talk this out, let’s talk this out. Don’t be so impulsive, I mean no harm." Feng Fang thought about how Lu Ming was about to take him to the Court of Justice, which would definitely alarm the Emperor.
He had finally managed to climb this ladder, becoming a captain in the Western Garden Army. If he worked diligently for a few years, he could basically rest easy.
Serving the Emperor was far better than being a lackey for powerful clans.
"Heh, you weren’t so principled before, Captain Feng!" Lu Ming’s eyes darted around, and he dragged Feng Fang into the main hall, ordering his personal guards to stand watch outside.
Inside the main hall, some meat had already been laid out.
In front of each prayer mat was a small table, one for each guest.
It seemed Feng Fang did indeed intend to host a banquet, but he didn’t know who he was inviting.

"Captain Feng, state your offer now, and I might consider it. If you don’t satisfy me, don’t blame me for being impolite!" Lu Ming was no longer flustered. As long as Emperor Ling feared death, he would never allow anything to happen to him.

Putting aside everything else, just relieving his pain and adding some specially made aphrodisiacs, allowing Emperor Ling to continue his nightly revelry and shorten his lifespan, was already quite generous.
Giving him the authority to lead an army independently and allowing him to return to Luoyang if necessary showed that they didn’t want anything to happen to him.
Otherwise, wouldn’t an emperor, even if he hadn’t killed a pig, have seen pigs run? Wouldn’t he know that generals couldn’t be separated by two people?
Knowing this and still doing it, there must be some unspeakable secret.
Even in Luoyang, rumors began to circulate that Lu Ming might be Emperor Ling’s illegitimate son, hence the preferential treatment.
Otherwise, there wouldn’t be such an outrageous order!
Even if he were on a campaign, being given the option to retreat at any time, and being able to claim it was an imperial decree to retreat, was unparalleled.
What the common people speculated about was irrelevant; the powerful families and nobles knew it was because of Lu Ming’s medical skills that they were giving him special treatment.
If he had simply been a doctor from the start, there would have been no problem.
But Lu Ming had been promoted based on military merit and entrusted with such an important position.
The patriarch of the Yang family, Yang Ci, was on the verge of death, but was miraculously saved!
Don’t underestimate this point; saving lives was secondary.
And because Yang Ci survived, the Yang family wouldn’t experience too much turmoil and could smoothly transfer power.
If things went wrong, and Yang Ci died kneeling before his political enemies, it wouldn’t just be the Yang family who lost face, but the public outrage!

These retired high-ranking officials were a symbol of power; they might not need to use it, but when they did, they were figures who made the entire city of Luoyang, and even the Eastern Han Dynasty, tremble.
With such a vivid example before him, Emperor Ling’s favor towards Lu Ming was no surprise; it was simply due to his exceptional medical skills.
Being a military general, leading troops in battle was his proper path, yet he had been forcibly transformed into a physician—this was quite absurd.
Using his medical skills to gain benefits, while also transcending the limitations of a physician, was very appealing; he wasn’t bound by such constraints.
Feng Fang racked his brains but couldn’t come up with a good plan. Just then, a flash of inspiration struck him, and he blurted out, "I wonder what Commander Lu thinks of my daughter?"
Before Lu Ming could speak, Feng Fang continued, "My daughter is quite beautiful, gentle, virtuous, and kind. I am currently preparing to find her a marriage partner."
Lu Ming was delighted. Was he being asked to marry Feng Qin?
It wasn’t impossible, but there was no such thing as a free lunch.

"Hmph, who knows if Wu Ban insulted her! You’re making a woman who has been insulted marry me, are you humiliating me! Or are you looking down on me! Hmph! Feng Fang, you’re courting death! I will report to His Majesty that since you don’t want to work anymore, there are plenty of people who will take your place!"
With that, Lu Ming made a gesture as if to turn and leave.

chapters.title: Chapter 163 Empress Dowager Dong’s buy-one-get-one-free offer
paragraphs: That night, Lu Ming pulled Cao Shi over, forcibly carried her to bed, and made both mother and daughter serve him.
After having sex with the daughter, he had sex with the mother, and then with the daughter, going on and on until both mother and daughter finally fell into a deep sleep.
Lu Ming, however, woke up after less than an hour, full of energy.
He turned to look at Cao Shi; her beautiful face, her hair clinging to her forehead, the sweat just dried, gave her a somewhat tragic beauty.
Beside her, Feng Qin was curled up in his arms like a kitten, seeking some security.
Getting up to tinker with the greenhouse, Lu Ming didn’t indulge in the pleasures of love.
Now was not the time to sleep. With his overlord’s body, he didn’t need much rest.
Unless his energy and mana were completely depleted, he wouldn’t need a longer rest.
Otherwise, he didn’t need a long rest; a short rest was enough to restore him to full strength.
Seedlings have already sprouted in several plots of land within the greenhouse, growing at an exceptionally rapid pace.
With the addition of special fertilizer, the four-day maturation time can be compressed to three days.
Normally, medicinal herbs grown outdoors take at least six months to yield any results.
Furthermore, because they are medicinal herbs, the actual profit is not high, far less efficient than growing grains.
Most medicinal herbs rely on wild harvesting, which is very limited, and suitable herbs are often difficult to find.
However, using the system’s built-in farmland, cultivation only takes seven days.
The greenhouse doubles the speed, adding approximately three days, and with fertilizer, it’s four days.
In total, plants mature in just three days.
This rapid pace allows him to accumulate a large amount of raw materials in a short time.
Using these herbs for himself or others is an excellent choice.
Especially in the treacherous city of Luoyang, it allows him to establish a foothold without worrying about future shortages.
As long as people fear death, they can remain invincible.
Where there is profit, there will be demand; this is the way of the world.
Treatment also requires medicinal herbs, and in the absence of them, cultivating them oneself is the most cost-effective option.
It’s the only way; there’s no other way.
He picked up his forged copper dagger and began whittling a small twig.
He started making wooden needles. Wooden needles have a limited number of uses, basically only three.
Silver needles, made from copper plates, have no limit on their use, but they are more precious, so he didn’t use them.
Firstly, they require smelting copper ore, and only self-smelted copper is effective.
Secondly, after the copper ore is smelted into copper, it needs a lengthy secondary processing to become copper plates.
Using a sharp copper knife to cut and create copper needles, and then smelting them into silver needles, is extremely troublesome.
Lu Ming made wooden needles only to thread them, storing enough needles and thread for future battles.
The method for training veterans is simple: more fighting, more bloodshed—that’s how you train new recruits into veterans.
But veterans were even more precious in ancient times because of poor medical conditions. Many injuries couldn’t be treated promptly, leaving soldiers to die.
Without sterilization, infection meant either amputation or certain death.
This drastically reduced the number of veterans, making them even more valuable.

Veterans could stabilize the morale of the army. If even one soldier collapsed, it could easily trigger a complete collapse. Veterans could maintain morale and lead new recruits to achieve formidable fighting power.
Since Emperor Ling had sent him on the expedition, Lu Ming certainly wouldn’t return empty-handed. He needed to acquire a decent army.
He could even bring them home later. After Emperor Ling’s death, the struggle between the eunuchs and General He Jin would intensify.
Even after the Wu Kuang incident, General He Jin remained aligned with the Yuan family.
Essentially, the eunuchs represented imperial power, while the Yuan family represented a powerful clan; this was a struggle between imperial power and aristocratic families.
The Ten Attendants and He Jin were merely representatives, with He Jin being a scapegoat pushed forward, ultimately leading to his demise.
Having made nearly a thousand wooden needles, Lu Ming began threading them again—a skilled task.
Each item he crafted granted him a small amount of crafting experience, though not much, it was better than nothing.
With more experience, he could sometimes achieve even greater results.

A twig could make four needles, but with experience, five could be made. The more experience he gained, the more needles he could produce, potentially doubling the number—that was the benefit of crafting experience.
However, for a lazybones like Lu Ming, his life was either filled with women or on his way to them.
It was quite unusual for him to be able to calm down now.
Meanwhile, Princess Wannian went to the palace early in the morning to meet Empress Dowager Dong.

Emperor Ling also spoke to Empress Dowager Dong about his intention to marry Princess Wannian to Lu Ming. He didn’t hold back, only mentioning his fondness for his youngest son, Liu Xie, and that Lu Ming’s ascension to the throne would allow him to build an army, preparing for the future.
Once Lu Ming married Princess Wannian, he would be on their side.
This was something Empress Dowager Dong couldn’t refuse, as her relationship with the Empress was consistently strained—not mortal enemies, but certainly extremely hostile.
If Liu Bian ascended the throne, the Empress would become Empress Dowager, putting her in a very difficult position.
According to custom and tradition, the eldest son ascending the throne was normal.
The appointment of a secondary heir required the Empress Dowager’s approval; such was the rule. Therefore, even if Empress He was being targeted, she couldn’t say anything openly.
Having Liu Xie ascend the throne was the best outcome. At least Liu Xie was far superior to Liu Bian.

"Wan Nian has been married before, and Lu Ming is so outstanding. I worry that he might hold a grudge later," Empress Dowager Dong said, understanding men all too well. While remarriage wasn’t uncommon for women, that applied to commoners. For those of high status, such considerations didn’t apply. Admittedly, it was a good thing, but what if Lu Ming rose to a high position? He might have reservations.
"Hmph! He wouldn’t dare!" Emperor Ling clearly hadn’t considered this, or rather, disdained to consider it. To him, a bestowed marriage was a great honor; how could Lu Ming dare to be picky!

Empress Dowager Dong, after a moment’s thought, added, "It’s rumored that the daughter of the great scholar Cai Yong has been widowed for a long time. Why doesn’t Your Majesty grant this wish and marry Cai Yong’s daughter to Lu Ming, marrying him off together? She and Wan Nian would be close friends, able to support each other. This would also provide them with external support within the scholarly community, which would be beneficial for Xie’er as well."

chapters.title: Chapter 164 Cai Wenji was also sold.
paragraphs: "Another widow? Hmph, he’s getting off easy. That brat has a thing for that kind of thing, always wanting to seduce other men’s wives and daughters, utterly despicable. Mother, you wouldn’t believe it, he even took Wu Kuang’s wife into his household! Hmph, utterly absurd!" Emperor Ling’s words, seemingly filled with disgust and anger, were actually a disguised expression of protection and affection.
If he didn’t like her, who would care about her life or death?
Empress Dowager Dong, however, felt a ripple of emotion. She was curious why a young man would enjoy playing with older women.
"With Wan Nian watching over her, things will be better. If Your Majesty is inconvenienced, how about I issue the decree?"

"Very well, then I’ll trouble you, Mother. When Wan Nian arrives later, Mother, you can have a good talk with her." Emperor Ling finished speaking and took his leave. It was better to leave this matter to the Empress Dowager.
"Your Majesty, rest assured, I will handle it properly." Empress Dowager Dong was very concerned about this matter, as it concerned her grandson’s ascension to the throne.
This also concerned her own wealth and status. Otherwise, after Emperor Ling died, there couldn’t possibly be two empress dowagers in the harem, and a grand empress dowager?
Would she still be an empress dowager?
She wouldn’t die in seclusion, nor would she be too far off. She had to stop this!
Without an empress dowager, her power as grand empress dowager wouldn’t be hindered!
Two hours later, Princess Wannian returned home angrily.
Initially somewhat unwilling, Princess Wannian had to accept it after a period of sulking. Even her father had spoken; what could she say?
Besides, Cai Yong’s daughter, Cai Wenji, was also marrying into the family. This wasn’t so bad for her; at least she had a close friend she could confide in.
Zhang Yulan and Cai Wenji came to the princess’s residence together. The three of them often studied the Book of Poetry together, or researched medicine, doing things they enjoyed.
Playing the zither, sipping tea—they lived a more comfortable life than many women.
Meanwhile, Cai Yong received an imperial edict from the Empress Dowager, betrothing his daughter to Lu Ming as a secondary wife.
At first, Cai Yong was somewhat shocked, only rising to thank her and accept the edict after being urged by the eunuch.
Even after the eunuch left, his head was still buzzing.
How could his daughter be betrothed by the Empress Dowager so easily?
The Empress Dowager did indeed wield such power; generally, she could arrange marriages for unmarried women.
However, this had little effect on powerful families, but it was very effective against the likes of Cai Yong and Huangfu Song.
These upright officials wouldn’t hold grudges; as long as it was an imperial appointment, they had to accept it, even if it meant refusing to listen.
Lu Ming, unaware that he had gained another wife, went to the training ground to check on the progress of his training over the past few days.
The soldiers were training diligently, hoping for a meal of meat.
Rice and meat were plentiful, which was a tremendous boon for most of the starving wandering knights.

Furthermore, facing elimination, and with Jiang Qin’s permission from Lu Ming to maliciously spread rumors that anyone eliminated would be punished by the remaining knights in Luoyang and the Guandong region, those eliminated were unlikely to return to their knightly lives.

With their escape routes cut off, they had no choice but to fight to the death. Benefits, no way out, and Jiang Qin’s leadership fueled a surge of fervent energy in this small contingent of five hundred recruits.

Standing on the training platform, Lu Ming looked at the soldiers below. They wore plain clothes, with only a few iron plates at the chest for protection; most were dressed in thin, inadequate clothing.
"I am Lu Ming, a junior officer in the Western Garden Army. I am also your superior. In a few days, we will be heading to Hedong to quell the rebellion. Are you afraid?"
Silence fell below, a slight commotion arose, but no one dared to utter a sound. Going to war in just a few days—wasn’t that suicide?
"I know you are afraid, and I know you don’t want to fight," Lu Ming chuckled. "I don’t want to fight either!"
This resonated with the wandering warriors below, though it might have affected morale, it was undeniably true.
Who wants to fight?
War means death. Isn’t it better to live well?
Better to live a wretched life than die. Nobody wants to die.

Seeing that the atmosphere had been built up sufficiently, Lu Ming abruptly changed his tone, saying, "But someone will always have to defend our country. Everyone is afraid of death. We all came out to achieve great deeds and benefit our descendants; we have no way back. To climb higher, we must stand on the corpses of others! And those rebels are our military achievements! Gentlemen, I cannot promise anything else, but I can promise one thing: if any of you die on the battlefield, your wives, children, and elderly parents will be taken in by me. Children will live to adulthood, and the elderly will live out their natural lifespan. I, as the Prefect of Longxi County, will allocate a piece of land in Longxi County for your families. They can cultivate the land and weave cloth, and I will take care of them until they can support themselves. A man’s word is his bond!"
This was incredibly explosive news. The people below couldn’t help but whisper among themselves; this way of caring for fallen soldiers was truly unbelievable.
"Silence! No whispering!" Jiang Qin, also somewhat fired up, trusted his lord and thus shouted.

Lu Ming stopped him, instead smiling and saying, "When I was suppressing the rebellion in Xiliang, I encountered an army of 100,000 rebels and still managed to take the enemy general’s head amidst a million soldiers. Following me is your good fortune; it’s hard to die even if you want to. In Luoyang, some call me ’the next Bian Que,’ which is actually a bit of a compliment. But I can tell you, as long as you are my soldiers, I will do my best to treat you until you die. You can ask me anything you want. After today, those who want to leave can leave; those who stay, do your best. If you rise to a high position one day, just remember my patronage."
The commotion below gradually subsided, for reasons unknown.

After waiting for a long time without anyone asking a question, Lu Ming scoffed, "What? You all used to be so high and mighty when you were wandering knights, but now you’re acting like cowards? I need soldiers, not cowards!"

"Sir! You said you’d support our families if we died in battle. That would cost countless sums of money. Do you have that kind of money?" a soldier asked boldly. This was his biggest concern, and the same question many others had about him.
Easier said than done, especially since this kind of task was thankless and costly, a complete waste of money. Besides, whether Lu Ming had the money was highly questionable!

chapters.title: Chapter 165 Cao Cao and Xiahou Yuan
paragraphs: Lu Ming clapped his hands vigorously, his expression relaxed. Even under the gaze of five hundred soldiers, he remained calm, showing no signs of panic or stage fright.

"Good question. I am honored by His Majesty’s favor and can assist him in managing some businesses. Your families can work in my textile factory. Children can deliver goods and gather firewood, women can weave cloth, and the elderly can enjoy their retirement. I provide a place where they can support themselves; they are essentially self-sufficient, so you have nothing to worry about."
Work hard to support themselves?
That was indeed a novel idea.
It was logical and convincing.
However, the details didn’t hold up to scrutiny; many other things were involved.
Simply managing businesses for His Majesty was already quite prestigious.
Anything associated with imperial power, even merchants, could elevate one’s status—that was the truth.
Imperial power is supreme; under heaven, the emperor is the greatest!
"How did you manage to take the enemy general’s head from among ten thousand soldiers, sir?" someone asked. With their worries resolved, the question was now about combat prowess.

Lu Ming twisted his wrist and said to those below, "It’s simple. One by one, I’ll knock you all down, and then you’ll know what I mean. Come on, whoever defeats me will be promoted to captain. Starting with you, line up from the back!"
Bang!
Before the first soldier could react, Lu Ming had sent him flying.
Then came the second, also knocked down in one move!
Purely relying on brute force in combat, if using the system template, it would be a one-hit kill!
Ah!
Ah!
Ah!
Screams rose and fell as Lu Ming, like a tiger among sheep, slaughtered his way through.

No one could withstand a single blow; those who managed to block one attack were quickly defeated in the second. The idea that military officers had infiltrated was wishful thinking; most of them were just thugs with little fighting ability.
Five hundred men, in less than an hour, were all defeated.

Lu Ming, twisting his wrist, strolled leisurely onto the arena. "If this were a battlefield battle, you would already be dead. If you want to live, train hard. Hone your skills, and follow me into battle. Whether you earn military merit, get promoted, and make a fortune depends on yourselves."
Now no one doubted Lu Ming. This elusive commander, whom they had only met twice, had already subdued these five hundred men. Everything seemed logical and convincing.
Not far away, a short, sallow-faced man stroked his beard, thoughtfully watching Lu Ming’s departing figure.
He felt a sense of apprehension, mixed with relief and disappointment.
This man was none other than Cao Cao. To fight alongside such a heroic figure was a rare and precious opportunity, yet there was a touch of disappointment: he couldn’t join him on this campaign.
"Wonderful talent," Cao Cao said, "how did such a man become? Defeating five hundred men single-handedly—such a feat could only be accomplished by a resurrected Xiang Yu!"

"Xiang Yu," Cao Cao was referring to, of course, the legendary Xiang Yu, the Hegemon-King of Western Chu. His exploits—the Battle of Julu, the decisive victory against overwhelming odds at Pengcheng, and even the escape of twenty-eight knights unscathed—all showcased his prowess.
But time was of the essence; with no hope of turning the tide, he chose to commit suicide at the Wujiang River.
This demonstrates that extreme bravery can indeed be admired.
Even someone like Lü Bu, with his personality and stature, had a large following. This is the benefit of bravery.
While powerful families might look down on someone they considered a mere brute, other members of the elite would undoubtedly see him as a worthy object of loyalty.
Miao Cai was Xiahou Yuan’s courtesy name.
Years ago, when Cao Cao was implicated in a case in his hometown, Xiahou Yuan took the blame for him.
Later, Cao Cao managed to rescue him, thus saving him from further trouble.
His relationship with Cao Cao was very close, and Cao Cao and the Xiahou family had intricate connections. His help stemmed not only from money but also from their fathers’ connections.
Xiahou Yuan watched Lu Ming leave with steady steps, showing no sign of weakness beneath his strength.
Even if those five hundred men were putting on a show, they couldn’t have acted so convincingly. Regardless, this was a capable man.
"This man is rumored to be able to take the head of a general from a million-strong army, but I don’t know if it’s true."
"We’ll wait and see!" Cao Cao was also looking forward to what this expedition would bring.
When Lu Ming returned to his residence, he saw his old acquaintance, Jian Shuo, who was also going to battle as a Colonel of the Upper Army.
Firstly, it was for oversight; secondly, it was to establish authority, and it was also Emperor Ling’s requirement.

Jian Shuo was probably one of Emperor Ling’s most trusted eunuchs, and he was somewhat different from others. The Ten Attendants were not a monolithic group; Zhang Rang and Duan Gui were one faction, while Jian Shuo and Zhao Zhong were another. Although the two factions had disagreements, there wasn’t any major conflict.
Besides being a favorite of Emperor Ling, Jian Shuo was also deeply trusted by Empress Dowager Dong.
This time, he came to read out Empress Dowager Dong’s imperial edict.

"By the Empress Dowager’s decree, Lu Ming, loyal to the Emperor and patriotic, recommended for his filial piety and integrity, has rendered meritorious service to His Majesty and the nation. Therefore, the daughter of the great Confucian scholar Cai Yong, Cai Wenji, is hereby bestowed upon Lu Ming as his secondary wife. This is the imperial decree!" After reading the decree, Jian Shuo immediately stepped forward with a beaming smile, saying, "Congratulations, Lord Lu! To be favored by the Empress Dowager is a truly great honor. I congratulate you on your marriage!"

Lu Ming felt somewhat bewildered, so he accepted the imperial decree, not forgetting to slip a jade pendant to her. "Thank you for your kindness, Lord Jian. May I ask what brings you to this wedding?"

"The wedding will take place on the day you return from Hedong, sir. She will marry you alongside Her Highness the Princess." Jian Shuo accepted the jade pendant with a smile, secretly feeling a pang of envy and jealousy. This favor was simply unparalleled! Unlike other eunuchs, although he admired Lu Ming, he wouldn’t harm him. Instead, he would try to cultivate a good relationship with him. Who knew if he might need him in the future? But a good relationship was essential!

"Thank you very much, Lord Jian. Please come into my humble abode for a drink," Lu Ming invited. Eunuchs were not to be offended, especially not now. When they held immense power, they were not to be offended; playing along was the best approach.

"No need for wine, I have other important matters to attend to. However, on your wedding day, I must come and ask for a cup of celebratory wine," Jian Shuo said with a smile. He clearly saw that Lu Ming had a bright future ahead of him; as long as he didn’t do anything reckless, he would be fine.
And the fact that His Majesty had turned a blind eye to his previous antics showed that his favor with the emperor had indeed reached a certain level.

Besides marital relations and responsibilities, truly wanting to have a child with a man who isn’t yet her husband can only be true love.
"Hmm, will the princess be jealous?" This was Lu Ming’s biggest concern.
He didn’t want his wife to be jealous; it was very bad.
And the best way to stop her from being jealous was to have sex with her, to fuck her hard, until she couldn’t control anything anymore.
"Hehe, of course not!
The princess is actually very kind and compassionate.
Husband, don’t worry.
With your abilities, you can definitely make her completely submissive.
No woman can refuse your manhood here!" Zhang Yulan finished speaking and forcefully tightened her vaginal muscles, causing the walls of her vagina to grip Lu Ming’s penis tightly a few times.
"Hiss!
You slut!" Lu Ming roared, aroused again.
Of course, another round of lovemaking ensued, leaving Zhang Yulan almost unable to walk.
With the departure for war approaching, Lu Ming spent almost every day at home playing with women, practicing martial arts, or doing some handicrafts.
The steward, Wu, reported that the shop was doing well.
Besides selling roasted mutton, Zhang Rang had also allocated some coal for them to sell, and there were other jobs available, enough to make him a fortune every day.
With his established reputation and Emperor Ling’s warning, no one dared to cause trouble.
The sons of noble families had all been instructed by their fathers not to provoke Lu Ming, at least not until the Yellow Turban Rebellion in Hedong was quelled and the army returned.
Otherwise, if Emperor Ling found an opportunity, he would confiscate their property, making them incredibly wealthy; no one dared to do that.
Taking this opportunity, Lu Ming also visited Wang Lang, who was about to leave for Xuzhou to take up his new post.
He was still quite interested in this famous figure who had clashed with Zhuge Liang on the battlefield and was so angered by his insults that he died.
However, Wang Lang was not impressed by Lu Ming’s arrival.

Although Lu Ming wasn’t responsible for the confiscation of his property, his wife and daughter had been taken by Lu Ming, and given the rumors he’d heard about Lu Ming’s penchant for raping other men’s wives and daughters, he assumed his own wife and daughters had been violated.
Therefore, he despised Lu Ming.
Lu Ming was also acting intentionally.
Having already violated another man’s wife and daughter, his visit to this aggrieved victim was bound to draw disdain.
Wang Lang, now appearing to be in his prime, still in middle age, would likely have already launched into a tirade if Yang Biao hadn’t been there.
Lu Ming was a distinguished guest of the Yang family, and Yang Ci’s tuberculosis treatment depended on Lu Ming’s help; therefore, he couldn’t be allowed to get into trouble.
The old man’s value lay in his life, thus Lu Ming held great value.
Yang Biao, after all, had to protect Lu Ming.
Summoning Lu Ming here was also to offer him some conveniences; once in Hedong, he could find Yang family vassals for assistance.
Whether it was military supplies or other matters, Lu Ming could help.
This was the advantage of social connections; curing an illness wasn’t a matter of a day or two, but required sustained effort.
A few days later, Lu Ming set off first.
He formed his own army, setting off with his five hundred men.
Before his departure, Zhang Rang specifically came out of the palace to tell him some things.
He was told that if things went wrong, he should flee immediately, as long as he didn’t die.
His survival meant Emperor Ling could live longer.
No other political exchanges were mentioned, but he was given the power to act expediently.
He could also allocate personnel from local garrisons to reinforce the Western Garden Army, a significant advantage.
Furthermore, he was given the power to incorporate the Yellow Turbans; everything could be handled on a case-by-case basis.
Otherwise, according to custom, rebellion meant death!

Except for a very few Yellow Turbans who were numerous and knew how to hide deep in the mountains and forests, making them impossible for government troops to suppress, anyone daring to appear on the plains and in county towns would have been wiped out long ago.
Letting Lu Ming go out now will ease the tense situation more.
Having offended the general and offended the Yuan family, even if Emperor Ling was there to protect him, it would be a disaster.
If you have some merit for coming out this time, plus Princess Wannian is getting married and has the status of a relative of the emperor, you have to think carefully before you want to touch him.
After leaving Mengjinguan, what comes into view is a rugged mountainous area.
Luoyang is a flat land in the middle.
Even in the suburbs, there is a large dirt road.
When we get here, the roads become bumpy and bumpy, and puddles will form after rainy days.
No one came to repair the road, not even the government.
Firstly, there was no money, and secondly, there was no benefit; no one would be willing to do such a thing.
Jiang Qin appeared exceptionally excited and solemn as he led his troops into battle for the first time.
This was it; whether he could achieve glory or not depended on this.
The soldiers, too, were somewhat apprehensive and extremely nervous.
They feared that a large force would suddenly appear and cut them down at any moment!
Actually, they were overthinking it.
Most of the troops were infantry, plus two hundred auxiliary soldiers used to transport supplies.
The combat soldiers were solely responsible for fighting; not separating them would only lead to a decrease in combat effectiveness.
No elite force could simultaneously perform manual labor and kill the enemy.
Lu Ming appeared particularly relaxed, constantly monitoring the map.
He was also continuously exploring.
Each exploration increased the progress of a map area and yielded resources, which were represented as cards.
These cards would appear in his hand upon collection, while others required a loading screen to collect.
For example, gathering ginger took half an hour, and chopping down small trees also required time.
Branches, wood, stones, and berries were displayed as cards on the map panel.

chapters.title: Chapter 172 There’s a mole, continue the transaction.
paragraphs: "Halt! The entire army, rest where you are!" Lu Ming suddenly shouted, taking a swig from a water pouch on his horse and gazing at the distant mountain peaks.

A mountain only five hundred meters high, its slopes covered in dense vegetation—ordinary trees, weeds, vines, and palm trees weaving a green tapestry that could easily disorient a rider and make it difficult to spot any ambushes.
"My lord, is something the matter?" Jiang Qin rode closer, asking softly. He keenly sensed something amiss, but couldn’t quite put his finger on it.

Lu Ming gestured towards the distance with his lip. "Gongyi, do you sense anything amiss ahead? Look, above the forest, birds are perched, not entering. There’s only one possibility: a flood or a ferocious beast! What could frighten birds so much that they wouldn’t enter the forest? Heh, there’s an ambush ahead! It seems someone leaked our marching route; someone’s prepared a great gift for us!"

"It was my oversight! Please punish me, my lord!" Jiang Qin exclaimed in alarm. He had clearly sent out scouts, yet they hadn’t detected it. If Lu Ming hadn’t pointed it out, their army would likely have suffered a severe defeat!
These new recruits, caught in an ambush, would surely be thrown into chaos!

"Gongyi, there’s no need for that. You’ve just joined the army and haven’t experienced the cruelty of war yet. Observe and learn more. A scholar should be viewed with new eyes after three days’ absence. I look forward to seeing you write your own military treatise after a hundred battles." Lu Ming was still lenient with his subordinates, patting him on the shoulder. "Self-criticism can wait until after the battle. Be patient in teaching them. There’s no need to be harsh on the soldiers. This is your first time, and it’s theirs too; it’s inevitable. Alright, now take two hundred men and quietly follow behind, circling around. When the fighting starts on my side, you launch a surprise attack from behind the enemy lines, a pincer movement that will surely throw them into chaos."
"Yes, my lord." Jiang Qin felt ashamed, but also more grateful and loyal to Lu Ming.
To have a righteous and discerning lord was an extremely fortunate thing for a subordinate.
After Jiang Qin left, Lu Ming’s eyes gradually turned cold. He had only just left Mengjin Pass.
There was an enemy ambush; he absolutely refused to believe there wasn’t a traitor!
Since they were here, he’d keep them all; he was just looking for some amusement.
He’d keep them alive, continue questioning them, find clues, and track them down to find the mastermind.
Meanwhile, on the low hill, two bearded, fierce-looking men were watching the Han army resting in the distance. Both were members of the White Turban Yellow Turbans.
A few days ago, someone tipped them off that a small Han army, carrying gold and silver treasures, was passing through here. They were only five or six hundred men, mostly new recruits.
They wanted them to rob this army, offering a small reward afterward.

If they had nothing to gain, they wouldn’t rob a government army. This place was only a short distance from Mengjin Port, still within Luoyang’s borders. Only after crossing the Yellow River did they realize the natural barrier of the Yellow River and Mengjin Pass; the Yellow Turban rebels had absolutely no chance of threatening Luoyang from here!
The reliability of this information has now been verified. As for the reward?
That depends on their mood.

"Heh, what a fat sheep! Look at those guys, so lax, they don’t even deserve to be called officers," Hu Long sneered, licking his lips. After this job, he’d go back to his stronghold and have some fun. What kind of government soldiers are they? They’re just trash that can be killed with a single blow!
"They stopped. Won’t they think we’re lying in ambush?" another burly man asked, sounding suspicious. A guilty conscience needs no accuser.

"Hmph, what’s there to be afraid of? Pang Bo, after this job, we’ll recruit more soldiers and become our own leaders. Do we still need to be controlled by others?" Hu Long wasn’t willing to let this fat sheep go. He didn’t care if they were government soldiers or not.
He was targeting government soldiers. They were already Yellow Turban rebels anyway; the strong fear the weak. Just do it!

The two were of one mind, clearly determined to rob Lu Ming. However, if someone told them that the leader of this army was the one who had killed Bian Zhang amidst a flurry of battle, would they still dare to ambush them?
After waiting for half an hour, seeing that Jiang Qin had already circled around to the designated position,

Lu Ming shouted loudly, "Everyone stand up! Prepare for battle! Grab your weapons! Auxiliary soldiers, retreat! Form ranks! Brothers, the time to make your mark has come! Ten coins per head! Kill ten, and you’ll be promoted to squad leader; kill a hundred, and you’ll be promoted to platoon leader! If you want wealth and glory, follow me!"
"Kill!"
"Kill!"
"Kill!"
Lu Ming’s roar ignited a surge of courage in the previously tense recruits. The fear and tension vanished after the roar.
One by one, they rubbed their hands together, picked up their spears and shields, and pressed forward step by step.
The bandits on the low hill panicked; the Han army had clearly spotted them.
"Damn it! We’ve been discovered!"
"They’ve discovered us! Who made that noise! Damn it!"
"At this point, we have no choice but to fight, or we won’t escape." Pang Bo knew something was wrong, but he’d been blinded by greed and wanted to make a quick buck. Now he’d lost everything.

"What’s there to be afraid of! There are only a little over three hundred of them. If we all attack together, we could drown them with a single spit! A thousand men against three hundred and they can’t even win? What’s the point of this game!" Hu Long cursed as he jumped out, brandishing his broadsword. "Brothers, charge! Kill them all! Loot all their silver! After this battle, I’ll give you rewards and women! Charge!"
Money and women are always the best way to boost morale.
The previously hesitant bandits immediately roared and charged down the mountain!
Charging downhill, the momentum of the charge could even cleave shields in two with a single blow!
Lu Ming took the lead, knowing he was key to boosting morale, and this was a crucial period, a fledgling stage where he needed to be hands-on.
"Insects, you dare to fight me? Your courage is commendable! But courage won’t save you! Die!"
*Thud!*

His spear pierced through a charging bandit soldier, the tip going through his throat, then sent him flying. He charged into the ranks like a tiger among sheep, and with the help of his personal guards, he was like a sharp sword breaking through the enemy formation.
"Kill!" Behind the bandits, Jiang Qin, also seething with anger, led two hundred soldiers out.
Faced with a pincer attack, the already weak-willed bandits immediately showed signs of collapse.

chapters.title: Chapter 173 Utter defeat
paragraphs: In ancient warfare, field battles were the most difficult because a unit would essentially collapse if its casualties exceeded 70%.
This was unavoidable; only a very few elite troops could fight to the death. Those who could hold out until more than 50% of their troops were considered elite!
Even the strongest elite troops are still human; they experience fear, and collapse is perfectly normal.
Even modern armies can collapse, let alone ancient armies.
Therefore, when Lu Ming and Jiang Qin launched their joint surprise attack, the Yellow Turban rebels already showed signs of instability.

With the wind at their backs, they were as strong as dogs; against the wind, they fled quickly. This was the characteristic of rebel troops; when they gathered in groups, they simply swarmed forward without any strategy or organization.
No wonder regular army officers looked down on the Yellow Turban army; to an expert’s eye, these rebels were not a threat at all!
"You scoundrel! Who do you think you are! Take this from General Tianlong!" Hu Long roared, slashing at Jiang Qin. He was enraged by being ambushed and surrounded.

If he lost this battle, even if he escaped, without soldiers, he would be nothing more than a dog, worse than dead. Internal factional infighting, coupled with all the enemies he had offended, would surely tear him to pieces!
Jiang Qin was a second-rate general, but even among second-rate, he was still top-tier.
Those with a martial prowess ranking between 80 and 90 were considered second-rate generals.
Even a second-rate general was a rare find, one in ten thousand, and still a formidable figure.
Therefore, seeing Hu Long dare to challenge him to a duel, he was overjoyed. He raised his broadsword to meet Hu Long head-on!
Bang!
Swoosh!

Jiang Qin remained unmoved, while Hu Long was forced back, his hand throbbing with pain, a trickle of blood seeping from the split opening. A single clash had been enough to split his hand; such strength was terrifying!
Before Hu Long had finished retreating, Jiang Qin stepped forward and, in Hu Long’s despairing eyes, cruelly severed his head!
"No!" Hu Long screamed as his head was decapitated. He held it in Jiang Qin’s hand, his consciousness fading into endless darkness.
Jiang Qin held Hu Long’s head, took a deep breath, and roared, "The bandit leader has been killed! Those who surrender will not be killed!"
Lu Ming severed Pang Bo’s right arm with a spear thrust, ordered his men to tie him up, and also roared, "The bandit leader is dead! Those who surrender will not be killed!"
Of the more than 1,200 bandits, only a little over 200 died before surrendering.
They lacked any backbone, and each one looked at Lu Ming with fear in their eyes, clearly terrified by his slaughter.
Despite wielding a long spear, he created a chaotic, fragmented spectacle, like a killing freak.

"Tie them up. Leave some to dig pits. Cut off the heads of the dead bandits; that’s our achievement. Bury the bodies on the spot to prevent plague," Lu Ming ordered, then took Pang Bo aside for interrogation.
This ambush would have been completely undetectable if he hadn’t seen the red dot on the map.
Who would have thought that bandits would ambush officers even within Luoyang territory!

"Yes, my lord," Jiang Qin, still somewhat fired up, ordered his soldiers to tie up the surrendered bandits to prevent them from surrendering again, and also instructed them to supervise the surrendered bandits in digging pits.
At first, the bandits hesitated, thinking they were being buried.
This wasn’t unprecedented; Dong Zhuo had done it before, and even Zhu Jun and Huangfu Song had buried prisoners alive.
Firstly, there wasn’t much surplus food, and secondly, these rebel soldiers were already inhuman, so killing them wouldn’t hurt, saving energy.
Jiang Qin also had his soldiers relay a message: they were only burying the dead, not burying them alive; they still had a chance to redeem themselves.
If they behaved well, they could even join the government troops and clear their names.
This statement made people somewhat skeptical; while they couldn’t completely believe it, it at least stopped them from having wild thoughts.
Pang Bo, with his arm severed, was sweating profusely from the pain; the blood at the stump had dried, making it look incredibly gruesome.

Lu Ming’s spear was pressed against his throat. "Who sent you? Tell me, and I’ll give you a quick death. I’ll spare your family; they don’t deserve to die. If you hide anything, or refuse to speak, I’ll kill everyone you know. Starting with your family, your brothers, cousins, uncles, and then your village—kill everyone you know, and finally, kill you!"
These vicious words stunned Pang Bo. The Han soldiers he’d fought before were never this ruthless.
They’d at most kill him outright; they never threatened him, never acted with such cruelty.

Looking into Lu Ming’s cold eyes, Pang Bo, sweating profusely, was at a loss for words. He moved his lips, and only after noticing Lu Ming’s impatient gaze did he burst into tears, wailing, "My lord, spare me! I truly didn’t know. Two days ago, someone delivered a message to our mountain stronghold, saying it was for me and Hu Long. It said that you, my lord, would be passing through here, and instructed us to ambush you, kill all the soldiers, and seize the gold and silver you were transporting. We really don’t know who it was, or who that person was, but it must be one of the powerful clans in Anyi City. There are only two powerful clans in Anyi City, the Jin clan and the Yang clan."
Lu Ming stroked his chin, unsure of the truth. If it was true, then it meant one of the two clans, the Jin or the Yang.

The Yang clan was a branch of the Hongnong Yang clan. The Yang clan had many branches, and these branches controlled a portion of the power in a region. Each year, they had to pay a substantial stipend to the clan, and outstanding individuals were recruited into the clan, enshrined in the ancestral hall, and worshiped by future generations.
"Hmph, I’ll spare your life for now. If you’re right, I’ll release you. Take him away." Lu Ming waved his hand, ordering his personal guards to take Pang Bo away.
He wouldn’t die anytime soon; if he did, so be it, he didn’t care.
Shortly afterward, the dead rebels were buried, and the wounded were bandaged.

Lu Ming then brainwashed these prisoners, promising them that if they behaved well, they would be rewarded with joining the government army to fight bravely. Upon returning to Luoyang, they could choose to stay or leave, or join his businesses to work and avoid starvation.
These weren’t unconditional; they had to earn them through hard work.
If they didn’t perform well, they would face beheading, after all, they were rebelling!
This was a capital offense!
It was perfectly reasonable, even flawless!
