We really don’t know who it was, or who that person was, but it must be one of the powerful clans in Anyi City.
There are only two powerful clans in Anyi City, the Jin clan and the Yang clan."
Lu Ming stroked his chin, unsure of the truth.
If it was true, then it meant one of the two clans, the Jin or the Yang.
The Yang clan was a branch of the Hongnong Yang clan.
The Yang clan had many branches, and these branches controlled a portion of the power in a region.
Each year, they had to pay a substantial stipend to the clan, and outstanding individuals were recruited into the clan, enshrined in the ancestral hall, and worshiped by future generations.
"Hmph, I’ll spare your life for now.
If you’re right, I’ll release you.
Take him away." Lu Ming waved his hand, ordering his personal guards to take Pang Bo away.
He wouldn’t die anytime soon; if he did, so be it, he didn’t care.
Shortly afterward, the dead rebels were buried, and the wounded were bandaged.
Lu Ming then brainwashed these prisoners, promising them that if they behaved well, they would be rewarded with joining the government army to fight bravely.
Upon returning to Luoyang, they could choose to stay or leave, or join his businesses to work and avoid starvation.
These weren’t unconditional; they had to earn them through hard work.
If they didn’t perform well, they would face beheading, after all, they were rebelling!
This was a capital offense!
It was perfectly reasonable, even flawless!

chapters.title: Chapter 174 Cut the weeds and eradicate the roots, leaving no evidence to prove otherwise.
paragraphs: Two hours later, in Anyi City.
In the Jin residence, a middle-aged man paced back and forth, clearly anxious.
Jin Kui, the head of the Jin family, was also a protégé of Yuan Kui.
He had risen to the position of Magistrate of Jingzhao through Yuan Kui’s connections, and later returned to Anyi City to inherit the position of family head.
He was a figure of immense prestige in the Anyi area.
Even the Yang family’s influence was overshadowed, and a few days ago, Yuan Kui had sent a letter instructing him to cooperate in eliminating Lu Ming’s detachment.
The Yellow Turban Rebellion appeared severe, but it ultimately harmed ordinary people.
Powerful families all possessed their own private armies, disguised as guards.
Manors were built like fortresses, with watchtowers and fortified villages, resembling small castles.
Therefore, no matter how fierce the Yellow Turban Rebellion became, it did not prevent them from indulging in pleasure within their estates.
Aside from the major cities, only the strong fortified villages in these areas were truly safe.
Smaller county towns were almost no match for the Yellow Turban Rebellion’s sweeping tide; they were quickly overrun, and their fate was death.
Shortly afterward, a servant rushed in and whispered, "My lord, they’ve failed. Hu Long has been beheaded, and Pang Bo has been captured."
"Who sent the message? Dispose of it." A dark glint flashed in Jin Kui’s eyes, and without hesitation, he acted ruthlessly.
He didn’t need to do anything; he just needed to ensure that everything was dead and without evidence. Killing Lu Ming to fulfill Yuan Kui’s request would be ideal.
If that wasn’t possible, then he would absolve himself. With no evidence, he couldn’t be harmed.
"Yes," the servant nodded, his Adam’s apple bobbing, but he didn’t say what he wanted to say, only responding in a low voice.
"You may leave now," Jin Kui waved for the servant to leave, and after a while, he summoned the steward.
"Master," the steward, Jin Teng, bowed respectfully. Stewards of large families were often bestowed with the family name, a privilege, a recognition, and the ultimate expression of a servant’s duty.

"Prepare the two thousand catties of millet we just harvested today, eight hundred winter coats, and a certain amount of ironware. When Colonel Lu Ming arrives in Anyi City, present these to him as a token of the Jin family’s goodwill, hoping he can quell the Yellow Turban Rebellion soon. That’s all. You may leave now." After giving his instructions, Jin Kui sat down again, picked up his teacup, took a few sips, and suppressed his inner unease.
He himself didn’t know why he felt this way. Perhaps Lu Ming’s fearsome reputation in Luoyang made him uneasy; otherwise, there was no explanation for his fear.
Lu Ming didn’t set up camp in the county town but instead chose a sheltered area to establish his camp.
That evening, people gathered around large bonfires.
Lu Ming began his speech, recounting how he survived in Xiliang, how his father was killed by bandits during a city siege, and how he climbed his way up step by step.
His story of a commoner’s rise to wealth resonated with the lives of most ordinary people.
It was also more likely to gain their approval. He told these tales to quickly win over the bandit soldiers and make them work for him.

This time, besides completing Emperor Ling’s mission, the main reason for their deployment was to expand their ranks. Being selected by the Yellow Turban Army proved these men were physically capable.
Furthermore, they had some combat experience, meaning they were no longer considered rookies.
With a little more training and more battles, they could grow stronger. Most importantly, they had no other choice. If they didn’t fight hard and earn military merit, death was the only outcome.
When death was certain, no one dared to carry out the mission, which would inevitably create negative consequences.
Once a chance to survive appears, it’s like a drowning person grasping at a straw—they desperately want to hold on and fight to live.
After stabilizing morale, Lu Ming began selecting soldiers from the ranks who met the system’s requirements for promotion.
His bravery was etched in their hearts; they admired him and were willing to submit. With loyalty and the system’s assistance, he wasn’t worried about their betrayal.
Moreover, the promoted soldiers were stronger, providing greater assistance.
"Thirty-five swordsmen and shieldmen, forty-seven sickle-wielders, thirty-seven archers, forty-five heavy guards, thirteen heavy axemen."
Looking at the numbers, it seemed small, but Lu Ming was already quite satisfied.
These were currently second-tier troops, the backbone of the force—significantly stronger, yet not too weak, perfectly suited as elite troops.

Looking at the job list, there’s a "Job Change" option above my head, allowing me to change jobs and experience them all. Each change grants attribute points and the opportunity to learn numerous spells and special skills, truly living up to my title of "Overlord’s Body"!

"Swordsman: Light Guard -- Heavy Guard -- Longswordsman -- Lieutenant General. General Follower Exclusive: Light Guard -- Heavy Guard -- Longswordsman -- Flying Dragon General. Special Branch: Light Guard -- Heavy Guard -- Ranger -- Sword Saint."
"Blade Soldiers: Swordsman -- Swordsman and Shield Soldier -- Light Cavalry -- Heavy Cavalry. General Follower Exclusive: Swordsman -- Swordsman and Shield Soldier -- Berserker -- Royal Guard."
"Archers: Archer -- Archer -- Longbowman -- Archer Cavalry" "Soldiers. General Follower Exclusive: Archer -- Archer -- Longbowman -- Sharpshooter."
"Axemen: Axe Warrior -- Heavy Axeman -- Great Axeman -- Axe Cavalry. General Follower Exclusive: Axe Warrior -- Heavy Axeman -- Great Axeman -- Iron General."
"Spearmen: Spearman -- Hooked Scythe Handler -- Elite Soldier -- Lancer. General Follower Exclusive: Spearman -- Hooked Scythe Handler -- Elite Soldier -- Tiger and Leopard Cavalry."
Looking at the template, there was even a healer. Lu Ming then looked at Jiang Qin’s troop type, but there was a slight change.
"Jiang Qin: Loyalty: 100, Class: Berserker (Water), Proficient in naval warfare."
Seeing this, Lu Ming stroked his chin. Did naval warfare have some effect? Would being unsuited for naval warfare lower his attributes? Perhaps. Seasickness was also normal.
He closed his eyes and began to explore this area.
With nothing else to do, he stepped out of his tent and began treating some of the wounded soldiers.
He treated even the captured bandits without discrimination.
In Lu Ming’s eyes, these were merely tools. To gain their loyalty, one must first learn to make them grateful.

chapters.title: Chapter 175 It is only natural to be grateful.
paragraphs: For large wounds, suturing with needle and thread is sufficient.
The unique suturing technique, combined with the fact that the fine fibers extracted from snake grass fall off after the wound heals, eliminates the need for stitch removal.
Furthermore, adding a herbal dressing accelerates the healing process. This herbal dressing is not difficult to make, only the process is somewhat complex.
First, the fibers are extracted, then twisted into fine ropes, and then the ropes are spun into a ball.
The ball of yarn is then processed on a prepared loom to obtain a piece of cloth.
The dressing is made from the ash of crushed charcoal. Combining the two creates the herbal dressing, which is particularly effective for external injuries, healing them almost within a few days.
However, this process accelerates the body’s own energy expenditure, a kind of energy conservation.
For fractures, splinting is sufficient, and healing takes about seven days, which is also very fast.
"A hundred days to recover from a broken bone"—this is no joke.
The medical devices created by the system could heal fractures within seven days—that was truly astonishing.
This was the benefit of the system: powerful yet simple.
Working until late at night, even Jiang Qin couldn’t help but urge Lu Ming to rest early.

Lu Ming waved him off, telling him to go rest first. He had things to assign him the next day—almost a mandatory order. Otherwise, Jiang Qin wouldn’t have left. In the Three Kingdoms period, a subordinate making their superior work overtime was an absolute disgrace, a sign of incompetence.
Lu Ming did this partly to win over his subordinates, and partly to quell his restless desires.
He was a lecher; he felt restless if he didn’t have sex with women for a day. It wasn’t that he would die without women.
It was an addictive symptom; he felt uncomfortable.
Smokers feel uncomfortable if they don’t smoke for a day.
And drinking coffee without smoking is similarly addictive; one feels restless if they don’t drink it for a day.
Sex addiction is similar; one needs sex every day, otherwise they feel unwell.
Unconsciously, both the lower-ranking soldiers and the captured bandits held Lu Ming in high esteem.
Such a hands-on general who cared for his soldiers like his own children was incredibly fortunate for them!
In other armies, bullying new recruits was commonplace; beatings and verbal abuse were the least of it. They would also steal the recruits’ food, clothes, and even their feet—it was all too frequent.

But the newly formed army didn’t have these bad habits. Coupled with a set of rules, officers were treated the same as soldiers in daily life, without any special privileges. They ate the same food as the soldiers.
They ate the same food, lived in the same lodgings, without any special treatment.

The goal was to create an atmosphere that rejected outdated practices. Considering that in other armies, even a general’s excrement was wiped by others, you can imagine the level of deprivation they endured.
No different from the nobles in Luoyang, this is how it is in wealthy families; otherwise, why would they be called "Master"?
It’s infuriating, but only because Lu Ming’s family isn’t particularly rich—they won’t starve, but they’re not wealthy either.
That’s why they don’t have such bad habits, and Lu Ming has forced them to grow grain on their fertile land, avoiding these kinds of frivolous things.
As dawn approached, Lu Ming, after only an hour’s rest, was full of energy, his steel spear practically piercing his crotch.
After tidying up, he took his personal guards out, and they began packing up the tents.
The entire camp proceeded with dismantling and packing in an orderly fashion, and the bandits captured the day before actively helped.
Considering they were half-dead when captured yesterday, their attitude had changed overnight—this was absolutely unbelievable.
Having witnessed Lu Ming’s actions, they knew that his promise to let them atone for their crimes through meritorious service was not a lie.
Not only could they be exonerated, but they could also join the ranks, and later even leave the army to live ordinary lives—this was simply a dream come true!

"It seems a completely new look has emerged in the ranks. Excellent, Gongyi, this is our foundation, the foundation for our achievements. No bad habits or humiliations can be brought in. Maintain this purity. I will have them transformed into an elite force, an invincible and unstoppable elite!" Looking at the vibrant army, Lu Ming felt a surge of pride and an urge to rule the world. A true man should indeed wield a sword and achieve unparalleled feats!
"Yes, my lord." Jiang Qin spoke little. To be able to join the army from a wandering swordsman, to follow a wise lord and achieve great things, was an immense stroke of luck.
In the words of a wandering swordsman, it was as if his ancestors’ graves were emitting auspicious smoke—only such good fortune could occur!
They marched onward, while Huangfu Song’s army set off behind them.
Their first stop was Anyi City, from where they would march north to suppress the rampant Yellow Turban rebels. This force, originating from Bai Bo, was formidable and had to be eradicated.
They had been subdued after Zhang Jiao’s defeat, but within a few years they were causing trouble again; they had to be wiped out.

Whether Zhang Chun, who was leading the rebellion in Bingzhou, was involved was unknown, but the purpose of this expedition was to suppress the Yellow Turbans in Hedong Commandery; supporting the suppression of the rebellion in Bingzhou was not a consideration.
Having arrived at Anyi City ahead of time, Lu Ming did not intend to confront the main Yellow Turban force head-on.
He simply wanted to observe from the sidelines, hoping to gain some advantage.
Therefore, he didn’t even enter Anyi City, but simply had his troops stationed outside.
He went in to meet with the local Yang family, obtaining some provisions, medicine, cloth, and equipment.
He didn’t even eat at the welcoming banquet and hurriedly left.

As he was about to leave the city, a wealthy-looking man dressed as a steward was already waiting at the city gate. Upon seeing Lu Ming, Jin Teng immediately stepped forward, smiling and bowing deeply. "Greetings, sir. I am Jin Teng, the steward of the Jin family in the city. I am here on my master’s orders to deliver provisions to you. This is the duty of the prefect, and also my master’s duty."
"Hmm, I understand. Where are the supplies?" Lu Ming didn’t stand on ceremony. Since they had come to his door, he might as well take them.

"They are already prepared outside the city. You can take them at any time, sir." Jin Teng listed the supplies item by item, from millet to vegetables and meat, salt was all available, and there were also some winter clothes. Although it was still late summer, the northern frontier was already quite chilly.

"Thank you very much. Please convey my thanks to your master. I have a servant here who claims to be from the Jin family, whom I rescued by the roadside. I’m returning him to you." Lu Ming clapped his hands after speaking, and his personal guards brought in the unconscious Pang Bo.
"The person is yours now, let’s go."

chapters.title: Chapter 176 There are experts
paragraphs: In the Jin family, Jin Kui is dealing with today’s affairs in the study.
As the governor of Anyi City, he usually likes to handle official business here.
I rarely go to the government office. The Jin family and the Yang family have the final say in Anyi City.
Yang is notoriously low-key and refuses to give up an inch in his position of power, but he is very restrained externally and has a good reputation.
Although the Jin family and the Yang family fought, they also lived in harmony.
Butler Jin Teng came in and reported today’s events, saying that everything was going well, except that Lu Ming sent someone over after taking away the supplies.
"Oh, a person? Who is that person?" Jin Kui had an ominous premonition, as if the other person had seen through something.

"Someone recognized a man with a broken arm. He was a small leader of the Yellow Turban remnants, named Pang Bo." The housekeeper didn’t know the dirtiness involved, so he restored the matter to its original form.
Jin Kui put down his pen and pondered for a long time, "Did he say anything if he wanted to take away supplies?"
"No, I didn’t say anything." The butler answered truthfully.
"Well, you can go down now." After dismissing the butler, Jin Kui sat in his seat and began to think.
Is this a temptation or a warning?
No matter what, the other party accepted his kindness.
Taking away the supplies means that the matter is not irreversible.
Thinking of this, he couldn’t help but breathe a sigh of relief. He was not afraid of anything else. He was just afraid that the other party would directly send troops to invade. That would be bad!
He remembered that after the duel between the other party and Wu Kuang, Wu Kuang’s son stepped forward to confront him, but was stabbed to death by Lu Ming. This was a complete killing!

Moreover, he also occupied Wu Kuang’s wife and daughter. The young cows could just eat the old grass. It is said that the men of the Wu family had a bad end and were sent to the palace to purify themselves and become eunuchs!
In fact, Jin Kui was overthinking, and Lu Ming had no evidence at all. Even if it was suspicion, it was just suspicion.
Without absolute certainty, he would not kill the Jin family.
Although it is fun to do it yourself, it is easy to leave clues.
After taking over the supplies, Lu Ming ordered the troops to continue moving forward.

At present, the Yellow Turban Army occupies Yicheng, which is considered a big city and is also located on a traffic artery. The Yellow Turbans with such obvious goals must obviously be left to Huangfu Song to deal with.
To capture a city, you need more than three times the number of troops, otherwise it would be a joke.
Not counting the prisoners at present, Lu Mingman had calculated that there were more than 400 people, and it was unrealistic to attack Yicheng.
He is currently wandering around, killing bandits and bandits, and writing a dozen travel notes.
There is no need to go head-on to the hard-steel Yellow Turban army.
If he could kill nearly 70,000 to 80,000 Yellow Turbans by himself, he would not gain much credit, but would be hated by others.
I’m not afraid of being jealous, but there’s no need to be the first to do it. It’s just a mess anyway, so I might as well do something else.

So Lu Ming led the team to march all the way to the north and stopped at a small county town two hundred miles away from Yicheng. It was close to mines and had rivers and lakes. However, it has now become a ruin. Only a few hundred people live here, all of them refugees from the ravages.
Regarding the arrival of the Han army, these refugees were a little trembling and shivering. The officers and soldiers were not necessarily much better than the Yellow Turbans.
Not far away, a group of caravans were besieged by bandits. They were fighting hard, and many of the caravan guards were killed. It seemed that they were in danger.
Lu Ming had just arrived with his army. He took a look and found that the civilians and caravans on the map were all yellow icons, representing neutrality.
The red dots are bandits and bandits. The Yellow Turbans are rampant and have spawned many bandits and bandits. If they can’t survive, they can only destroy their homes and rob their homes.
"The whole army is here, ready to attack, come with me!"
Without the slightest hesitation, Lu Ming led his army and launched a charge.
This time, he came out to develop his own technology.
Finding a place with good resources and environment to forge materials and make knives is a very good choice for him.
You can continue to lead this team in the future, and you can catch fish when you go out to catch fish, but you can’t stop improving yourself.
"Boss, officers and soldiers are coming!" A bandit shouted in horror.

"Fart! The officers and soldiers have run away, where did the officers and soldiers come from!" Just as the sturdy bandit leader finished speaking, an arrow flew from a distance and shot straight through his throat. He didn’t even have time to react.
Lu Ming put down his compound bow, then picked up his spear, "Lieutenant Lu Ming of the Xiyuan Army is here. Put down your weapons and surrender. Those who surrender will not be killed!"

"What are you bragging about! Who are you! I don’t know you at all!" He stabbed a caravan guard to death with one shot. The man roared angrily and charged forward with his horse. At the same time, he roared angrily. His voice was thunderous and powerful, and his horse riding pace was very skillful. He didn’t look like an ordinary person at all.

Lu Ming’s eyes flashed, and he charged fiercely, grazing the opponent’s spear tip with his spear and thrusting at him. He tried to dodge the opponent’s thrust, but found that it was useless, so he stopped dodging and stabbed him head-on!
"Madman!" The man screamed and tried to run away, but it was too late! The tip of the spear pierced Lu Ming’s armor, and he was stabbed to the core by the other party!

After being stabbed, the blood volume of more than a thousand people suddenly dropped to more than 800. Lu Ming just frowned slightly and used a medical technique on himself to increase the blood volume.
Then he pulled out the tip of the gun and slapped the opponent to the ground with one stroke. The gun barrel continuously slapped the opponent’s hands into pulverized fractures!

Without blinking an eye, he then went on a killing spree, killing these bandits until they cried like ghosts and howled like wolves. Rivers of blood flowed and heads rolled. The remaining bandits didn’t even have the courage to escape. They could only kneel down and beg for mercy, their bodies shaking constantly due to fear.
Lu Ming’s appearance is really too scary. Anyone who sees it will be frightened and frightened. Is this a fucking centaur?
"Lord, are you okay?" Jiang Qin rushed over. Seeing this scene of blood flowing into a river, he couldn’t help but feel a little numb. This was too cruel!
"It’s okay. Send someone to collect the corpses and gather these prisoners. It will be of great use." Lu Ming waved his hand, took out a needle and thread and sewed it up directly for himself.
To outsiders, it may seem like the scalp is numb, and the pain of using a needle to prick the skin is too painful!
Then take out the plant dressing and cover it to avoid bacterial infection and speed up wound healing.

"Yes, my lord." Jiang Qin admired Lu Ming more and more. This lord’s force value was astonishingly high, and he also ran the army rigorously. He had never seen an army without orders and prohibitions.

chapters.title: Chapter 177 Zhen Yao’s request for help
paragraphs: This little skin injury is nothing to Lu Ming. As long as it heals, there will be no scars left, which can be regarded as a benefit given by the system.
And he has a diamond body protection, so he won’t bleed. He just needs to speed up the healing of the wound, because the blood volume can be lifted up, and the wound will be very painful.

The person in charge of the caravan was a bearded man dressed like a scholar. He came over and bowed deeply to Lu Ming, "Thank you, general, for saving me. I’d like to ask Zhen Yao, the governor of Wuji County in Zhongshan."

"I am your Majesty’s newly formed personal army, one of the eight captains of Xiyuan, the captain of the lower military and the governor of Longxi County, Lu Ming." Lu Ming also returned the greeting. After hearing the other party’s name, his eyes narrowed slightly, and a flash of sharpness flashed, "Since you are from the Zhongshan Kingdom and are far away in Jizhou, why did you come to Hedong?"
The Zhongshan Kingdom is still called a kingdom, not a county.
The princes of the Han Dynasty will be enfeoffed and become princes, which is called opening the country and establishing the country.
Therefore, Zhongshan County is only to become Zhongshan Kingdom, just like Changshan County is currently also called Changshan Kingdom.

Zhen Yao compiled calmly, "It’s because of Niu Po, the governor of Chengyicheng. The two places are well connected in trade. I received rumors a few days ago, so the governor of Wuji assigned me to escort weapons, armor, and grain and grass to support Yicheng."

"Yicheng has now fallen and is occupied by the White Wave and Yellow Turbans. Your trip is just like a sheep entering a tiger’s mouth. You leave the supplies. I, under His Majesty’s orders, will lead the army to suppress the rebellion, and have the power to do things conveniently. Once you have a letter from my captain, you can take it back and deliver it." Lu Ming unceremoniously took this batch of supplies as his own. Anyway, Yicheng has fallen and the things cannot be sent in, so he will keep them for him to use.

"Sir, I’m afraid this is against the rules, isn’t it?" Zhen Yao hesitated a little. The other party was obviously trying to plunder something. If this batch of supplies was lost, it would be troublesome if the Zhen family was blamed.

"Your Zhen family is also an aristocratic family in Zhongshan. What’s there to be afraid of? Who dares to blame you? Let him come to Luoyang to find our captain. Okay, leave your things behind and you can leave and go back to deliver the goods. The war here is chaotic, so don’t stay any longer." Lu Ming was not polite and took it down first. He thought it was a caravan, but it turned out to be a team escorting supplies.
Zhen Yao couldn’t force himself, so he could only order his subordinates to transfer the supplies to this army.
"Sir, the people who attacked just now are from the tribe of the Southern Xiongnu. They colluded with the Black Mountain Yellow Turbans and repeatedly violated our borders and disturbed the people."
"Oh, no wonder the martial arts are pretty good right away. I know that Captain Zhen has something important to do?" Lu Ming could see that the other party seemed to want to exchange something.
He didn’t mind making a deal with the other party. The Zhen family in Zhongshan was indeed a wealthy family, and Zhen Yao was the chief registrar, but his father was still the county magistrate.
The Zhen family is also a wealthy business family. They have thousands of acres of fertile land and tens of thousands of slaves. They are truly a wealthy family.
Moreover, the official position with a hereditary salary of two thousand stone in the family is not nothing.
Otherwise, Yuan Shao would not have allowed his son to marry the Zhen family, and there are explanations for that.
A well-matched family means a well-matched family, and the water here is very deep when marrying down and climbing up the ladder.
If it is really a mismatch, a woman will be tortured to death if she marries. At this point, what needs to be considered is the prosperity of the family, not the so-called love.
But, Lu Ming has no intention of following these bullshit rules.
Rules are a product of the peaceful and prosperous times.
And troubled times are coming, and then fists are power.
The only thing that aristocratic families rely on for their survival is that their children are all scholars and can do things that ordinary people cannot do, such as handling government affairs.
Ordinary people don’t even know the words, so naturally it’s impossible for them to do these things. This is a kind of monopoly, monopolizing all the upward channels.
Emperor Ling married Cai Wenji to him, so Cai Wenji’s father was a learned scholar, so it was obviously a good choice to let him teach.
Cultivating talents by oneself and not relying on others is the source of confidence.
Therefore, Lu Ming disdains these bullshit rules.
But what really moved Lu Ming was the legendary beauty Zhen Mi, known as the Goddess of Luo.
Haha, since I am already a lustful ghost, if I don’t collect beauties, I will be sorry for myself.

Zhen Yao really wanted to ask for something, so he said in a low voice, "Sir, this beast is related to the Bingzhou rebellion and is also related to the Black Mountain Yellow Turban. If you can defeat this unit, it will be a great achievement for you!"
This is a plan to do nothing. If it is a great achievement, it must be recognized by the superiors and rewarded. That is a great achievement.

Therefore, Lu Ming directly interrupted the other party’s speech. Although it was very rude, the other party was scheming first, "Okay, these are none of my business. What do you want from me and what bargaining chips can you bring? Just tell me directly. I have seen many intrigues in Luoyang."
Zhen Yao was a little angry, and his impression of Lu Ming became even worse.

But he had no choice but to endure it, because if he didn’t solve any problem, his return would be a problem. Whether he could go back alive or not was left to fate. It would be much safer to let Lu Ming take action and defeat the entrenched rebels.

"Sir, this rebel army is in Anze in the north. Together with the Southern Xiongnu, they looted, killed and set fire to people. Countless villages were destroyed and the people were displaced. If you can wipe out that rebel army, I would like to give you a hundred gold."

"Haha, this rebel army must be at least ten thousand people. How can you let me take action with such a small amount of money? Master Zhen, you can’t be too stingy. You should have heard a saying that the most uncomfortable thing in this world is that the money is still there but the people are gone." Lu Ming patted the other party’s shoulder, turned around and left, feeling petty.
"A common man!" Zhen Yao cursed in his heart, but did not dare to say anything more.
He can’t afford much money now, and he really doesn’t have many chips in his hand.
But if Lu Ming doesn’t help him, he won’t be able to go back. This is really an insurmountable problem.

"My lord, my lord, it’s better than this. If your lord can send me to Shangdang County, my family still has some assets in Shangdang County, and I will definitely give you a surprise." Zhen Yao could only retreat and find another way.

chapters.title: Chapter 178 Zhen Yao’s last bargaining chip
paragraphs: "It’s a long way to go to Shangdang County, and the mountain road is difficult to travel. You can’t reach it in less than twenty days. Master Zhen, you’d better go back by yourself." Lu Ming will not be fooled. Do you really think you will give money when you get there?
Surprise?
Why the hell don’t you just say what a surprise is?
The army rested in place, set up tents, set up camps, made fires to cook, and treated the wounded.
Lu Ming pulled the prisoner with disabled hands aside and began to interrogate him. He did not need to ask directly, he only needed to use skills.
There are many branches in the espionage skill tree, including interrogation, intimidation, instigation of rebellion, rumors, incitement, torture, etc.

At the beginning, there is only the option of cross-examination. The information obtained through this option varies from person to person. If the other party does not say anything, there is no way to obtain the information.
And if you have a weak character, you may confess.
Half an hour later, there was no good piece of meat on the prisoner’s body, and all of them were cut to pieces by Lu Ming.
Lu Ming wiped the bloody dagger clean on the opponent’s clothes. Lu Ming already knew the identity of the prisoner.
I thought he was a famous general, but I thought too much.
The other party turned out to be a big fish!
A pretty big fish!
Just a big fish without much profit!
Kaku Gu, the son of the Xiongnu Chanyu of the Southern Xiongnu, and one of the sons of Yufuluo.

Yufuluo was a Xiongnu Chanyu who led troops to the Central Plains to assist the Eastern Han Dynasty in suppressing the Yellow Turban Uprising. He caught up with the rebellion in his own country and his father was killed. So he stayed in the Central Plains and joined forces with the Baibo Army to plunder Taiyuan, Hedong and other places.
Now they have turned into bandits. No matter whether they are forced to do anything or they have such intentions, they cannot escape the relationship.
In history, Cai Wenji was kidnapped because of them.
"Ding, triggering branch information, no reward."

"Side intelligence: Dong Zhuo’s subordinate Zhang Ji sent someone to transport his family and his wife, Zou, to Bingzhou. Passing through Hedong County, they were targeted by the rebels entrenched in Anze County."

In addition, Lu Ming can also see the route of a convoy on the map. And on the map, the location of Anze County is only about two hundred miles away from here. It is indeed not far, but it is not close either.
Seeing this, Lu Ming looked at the information.
This is intelligence, not a mission.
Currently, there are almost no tasks for myself, the most is information.

How you use the information after you have it is your own business. You can choose to use the information to seek benefits, or you can use the information to turn a deaf ear and pretend that nothing happened.
Now that Zhang Ji’s family is being targeted by the rebels, it means there is much more danger.
He can completely ignore it. Even if something happens, he will not be blamed.
And if you save Zhang Ji’s family, you will definitely get Zhang Ji’s thanks.
These are the two choices, to save or not to save.
However, Lu Ming simply ignored these two options and chose the third one. Kill someone with a borrowed knife and then take it for yourself!

Normally speaking, there are two choices: to help or not to help. But what Lu Ming wanted to do was to let the rebels kill almost all the private guards sent by Zhang Ji, and then take action himself, pretending not to recognize them, and then take the Zou family as his own!

Even if Zhang Ji knew about it, he could pretend not to know her, because he had never met Zhang Ji’s wife Zou before, and it could be said that it was a trophy obtained after killing the rebels, implying that Zou had been captured by the rebels.
And if a woman is captured, will she still be intact?
While making Zhang Ji sick, he still doesn’t blame himself. This is simply killing two birds with one stone!
I will not offend Zhang Ji, and I can get the Zou family legally!
This is simply killing two birds with one stone, eating two fish with one fish!

And the most important thing is that the Zou family also left a strong mark in history. After Zhang Xiu surrendered, he was taken in by Cao Cao. As a result, Zhang Xiu rebelled, Cao Cao defeated Wancheng, Cao Ang, Dian Wei, Cao Anmin died in battle, and many other things.
Being able to make Cao Cao kill a general, a son, and a nephew to get her is considered a legendary woman, which shows how beautiful she is.
Looking at the signs on the map, Lu Ming had a plan in mind. So he went out to gather the soldiers, and happened to meet Zhen Yao again, who stuck to him like a dog-skin plaster.
"What’s the matter with you? Leave quickly. This is a powerful military camp. No outsiders will be left." Lu Ming didn’t want to live with someone like this who couldn’t do anything good.
It’s not that the other party is poor. If he is a poor guy who can’t squeeze out any money, even if he is forced to do so, he can’t get it out, so that means nothing!

But Zhen Yao was different. He relied on the Zhen family, which was a big business, and it was also a business and official family. To spend a hundred gold to send him away, what is the difference between sending him away and sending him away as a beggar?
Since you think of him as a beggar, don’t blame him for being rude!

How could Zhen Yao dare to leave? He still had something to say, that is, the Black Mountain Yellow Turbans had blackmailed the aristocratic families around Jizhou, and the Zhen family was naturally no exception.
The Zhen family refused to give money, and other families also refused to give money. As a result, the Yellow Turban rebels captured the city and captured the land, leaving not even a tomb behind.
Now if you want to give money, you have to double it several times, almost giving one-third of the Zhen family’s property. How is this possible!

If you are riding a tiger and it is difficult to get off, you don’t have to worry if you are in Wuji County. If the Yellow Turban rebels come over, they can be let in vertically and carried out horizontally.
But aristocratic families don’t just rely on these, they also have to circulate, make money, and have contacts.
If it is attacked and plundered every time, the power will be damaged.
Therefore, there are only two ways before us, either compromise or destroy the Yellow Turbans.
It’s just the Black Mountain Yellow Turbans, even the imperial army can’t destroy them.
Most of the Taihang Mountains are deep mountains and old forests. You don’t know how you will die if you go in. It is easier said than done to eradicate them!

"Sir, I can write a letter and ask the nearest trading house to prepare three thousand catties of corn, five hundred catties of meat, one thousand gold and silver, and a beauty to give to you. I just ask you to take action and annihilate the rebels in Anze County." Zhen Yao had no choice but to maximize his bargaining chips.

"Oh? Okay, just let them prepare it. I will go and get it myself, and when I get the things, I will take action. You can go to Luoyang to find out. I can’t keep up with my words. I pay with one hand and deliver the goods with the other hand. I am a good boy!" Lu Ming was a little surprised. Since you can eat two fish, you can also eat three fish.
Besides, these things are the best if they are available, and it doesn’t matter if they are not available.

sentences.text: "It’s a long way to go to Shangdang County, and the mountain road is difficult to travel.
You can’t reach it in less than twenty days.
Master Zhen, you’d better go back by yourself." Lu Ming will not be fooled.
Do you really think you will give money when you get there?
Surprise?
Why the hell don’t you just say what a surprise is?
The army rested in place, set up tents, set up camps, made fires to cook, and treated the wounded.
Lu Ming pulled the prisoner with disabled hands aside and began to interrogate him.
He did not need to ask directly, he only needed to use skills.
There are many branches in the espionage skill tree, including interrogation, intimidation, instigation of rebellion, rumors, incitement, torture, etc.
At the beginning, there is only the option of cross-examination.
The information obtained through this option varies from person to person.
If the other party does not say anything, there is no way to obtain the information.
And if you have a weak character, you may confess.
Half an hour later, there was no good piece of meat on the prisoner’s body, and all of them were cut to pieces by Lu Ming.
Lu Ming wiped the bloody dagger clean on the opponent’s clothes.
Lu Ming already knew the identity of the prisoner.
I thought he was a famous general, but I thought too much.
The other party turned out to be a big fish!
A pretty big fish!
Just a big fish without much profit!

He caught up with the rebellion in his own country and his father was killed.

Now they have turned into bandits.
No matter whether they are forced to do anything or they have such intentions, they cannot escape the relationship.
In history, Cai Wenji was kidnapped because of them.
"Ding, triggering branch information, no reward."
"Side intelligence: Dong Zhuo’s subordinate Zhang Ji sent someone to transport his family and his wife, Zou, to Bingzhou.
Passing through Hedong County, they were targeted by the rebels entrenched in Anze County."
In addition, Lu Ming can also see the route of a convoy on the map.
And on the map, the location of Anze County is only about two hundred miles away from here.
It is indeed not far, but it is not close either.
Seeing this, Lu Ming looked at the information.
This is intelligence, not a mission.
Currently, there are almost no tasks for myself, the most is information.
How you use the information after you have it is your own business.
You can choose to use the information to seek benefits, or you can use the information to turn a deaf ear and pretend that nothing happened.
Now that Zhang Ji’s family is being targeted by the rebels, it means there is much more danger.
He can completely ignore it.
Even if something happens, he will not be blamed.
And if you save Zhang Ji’s family, you will definitely get Zhang Ji’s thanks.
These are the two choices, to save or not to save.
However, Lu Ming simply ignored these two options and chose the third one.
Kill someone with a borrowed knife and then take it for yourself!
Normally speaking, there are two choices: to help or not to help.

But what Lu Ming wanted to do was to let the rebels kill almost all the private guards sent by Zhang Ji, and then take action himself, pretending not to recognize them, and then take the Zou family as his own!

Even if Zhang Ji knew about it, he could pretend not to know her, because he had never met Zhang Ji’s wife Zou before, and it could be said that it was a trophy obtained after killing the rebels, implying that Zou had been captured by the rebels.
And if a woman is captured, will she still be intact?
While making Zhang Ji sick, he still doesn’t blame himself.
This is simply killing two birds with one stone!
I will not offend Zhang Ji, and I can get the Zou family legally!
This is simply killing two birds with one stone, eating two fish with one fish!
And the most important thing is that the Zou family also left a strong mark in history.
After Zhang Xiu surrendered, he was taken in by Cao Cao.
As a result, Zhang Xiu rebelled, Cao Cao defeated Wancheng, Cao Ang, Dian Wei, Cao Anmin died in battle, and many other things.
Being able to make Cao Cao kill a general, a son, and a nephew to get her is considered a legendary woman, which shows how beautiful she is.
Looking at the signs on the map, Lu Ming had a plan in mind.
So he went out to gather the soldiers, and happened to meet Zhen Yao again, who stuck to him like a dog-skin plaster.
"What’s the matter with you?
Leave quickly.
This is a powerful military camp.
No outsiders will be left." Lu Ming didn’t want to live with someone like this who couldn’t do anything good.
It’s not that the other party is poor.
If he is a poor guy who can’t squeeze out any money, even if he is forced to do so, he can’t get it out, so that means nothing!

chapters.title: Chapter 179 Third option
paragraphs: "In that case, I will write a letter, and it will be ready within three days. Please go to Yangcheng, sir, to obtain it; I can also go there myself." Zhen Yao had no other choice. He could only take a detour, albeit with a smaller contribution. Being targeted was like having thorns in his back. There’s no such thing as a thousand-day defense against a thief, even if you’re careful. A single oversight could eventually be exploited, making it a losing proposition.

"Alright, go write the letter. I’ll send you to Yangcheng in three days. Once I’ve wiped out the Yellow Turbans in Anze County, you can travel in peace." Lu Ming had no particular interest; since the price was acceptable, he’d do the deal.

"Thank you, sir. I’ll take my leave now. But could you allow me to station my guards nearby to prevent any bandit attacks and to create a pincer movement?" Zhen Yao still felt pressured. At least after witnessing Lu Ming’s godlike performance and battlefield rampage, following this brute seemed safer.
Scholars, however, always looked down on such brutes—mere muscle-bound fools!
They certainly wouldn’t say it aloud; their contempt was none of the other party’s business.
Leading over a hundred personal guards, all of whom had undergone rank changes, Lu Ming set off.

Before leaving, he called Jiang Qin aside and instructed him to send out scouts to monitor the Yellow Turban movements. If the Yellow Turbans in Yicheng mobilized, then he should lead his men north to rendezvous with him.

"Profession: (Tiger and Leopard Cavalry) Archer, Special Skill: None. Level: Five. Experience: Thirty. Trait, Marching: Increases the movement speed of the commander’s troops by 100%, ignoring terrain obstacles."
Having one’s own personal guards provides this advantage; speed is crucial in both ancient and modern warfare.
It’s like two masters dueling; Chu Liuxiang slapped the Fire Cloud Evil God and ran far away, while the Fire Cloud Evil God only reacted after punching thin air—that’s the key to speed.
Without any hindrance, Lu Ming’s speed was phenomenal.
The group of over a hundred people traversed mountains and valleys, encountering numerous wild animals along the way.
With both hands, he shot arrows, each venomous snake a kill, and even managed to kill several wild boars, which Lu Ming stored in his medicine box.
It would keep them fresh and prevent them from spoiling.
In their haste, they didn’t bother processing the corpses; they could prepare them later when needed.
Lu Ming led the group, covering a distance of two hundred li (approximately 100 kilometers), completing the journey in just one hour, despite the arduous mountain crossing.
Even Xiahou Yuan, renowned for his long-distance raids, would blush at this speed—it was simply inhuman!
The nature of marching was purely about maximizing stamina for combat, so there was no worry about running out of energy after such a rapid march.
Meanwhile, in the distance, a convoy of carriages was slowly making its way.
The bumpy, muddy road was a typical scene in ancient times; cement hadn’t been invented yet, let alone paved roads.
Only in large cities can you see roads paved with blue bricks; everywhere else, they’re mostly dirt roads, some even mixed with sand and gravel—much better than traditional muddy roads.
Lu Ming distributed insect repellent cream. Applying a little to exposed skin would keep mosquitoes away.
This cream, made from aloe vera and snake grass, lasted for about ten hours. As long as it wasn’t washed off, the effect was excellent.

Mosquitoes were the most annoying thing in the wild. The mosquitoes in the mountain gullies were extremely venomous and easily spread diseases. Too many bites could cause overheating, which could even be fatal.
It was necessary to boost immunity to suppress them; there wasn’t a very good, effective medicine.
Therefore, personal protection was crucial at this time. It was their foundation, so they naturally had to be extra careful.
In the distance, a group of sneaky bandits began to lie in ambush.
Among them were even quite a few cavalrymen, their faces painted with strange camouflage—undoubtedly the style of the Huns.
Zhen Yao’s statement that the Southern Xiongnu had allied with the Yellow Turban rebels seemed to be true.
Lu Ming had never had a good impression of the invading Xiongnu.
Just like no one likes invading Japanese pirates, those bastards should stay in their own territory.
If they insist on making a fool of themselves, then they’ll just have to be taught a small lesson.
Zhang Ping was a seasoned captain who had accumulated numerous merits in battles since Zhang Ji joined Dong Zhuo.

However, due to his humble origins, even though his military career was more fortunate than most, he was still only a lowly captain. This was nothing like a captain appointed by the court; he wasn’t even qualified to carry shoes.
This time, ordered to escort his cousin’s wives and concubines to Bingzhou, his eyelids kept twitching; he had a very bad premonition.
Bingzhou wasn’t actually far from here; after all, Bingzhou was just outside Hedong Commandery, and it was a direct route from Liangzhou.
The risk of going through Hedong Commandery was much, much lower; a direct route would be disastrous if they encountered Xiongnu or Wuhuan cavalry.
"All of you, stay alert! You can rest when it’s time. If you slack off, I won’t be so lenient!" Zhang Ping shouted to bolster his courage; the atmosphere here was truly eerie.
High mountains on both sides, with a river running alongside—this kind of road was easy to ambush.
However, they weren’t transporting any valuables, and their armor clearly identified them as government troops. If someone came to rob them, wouldn’t they be asking for trouble?

Inside the carriage, a beautiful, mature woman, seemingly middle-aged yet showing no signs of age, sat gracefully. Her gentle demeanor, exquisite face, and delicate curves, along with her full, rosy lips, made one want to embrace her and kiss her passionately.
The elegant silk draped around her jade-like neck, revealing not a trace of skin, yet still exuding an alluring charm.

Her captivating allure, emanating from within, irresistibly drew men closer. Even with her lips tightly pressed together, feigning seriousness, a cool, repressed allure remained. Her natural temperament (qi zhi, a kind of refined elegance or aura) defined her as a woman of inner beauty, a sophisticated mature woman who knew how to seduce men perfectly!
Through a woman’s intuition, Zou sensed something amiss.
She and Zhang Ji rarely saw each other, and this trip was likely due to a prolonged stay in Bingzhou, hence the invitation to bring her along.
No explanation was given, nor was one necessary.
To a woman, she was merely an object, a tool for sexual gratification. A woman without status or position was simply a tool for satisfying lust and procreation, nothing more.

chapters.title: Chapter 180 The final kick
paragraphs: Han Xian, looking annoyed, sat in the forest staring at the distant carriage. Suddenly, he slapped his thigh hard, raising his hand to find it covered in blood.
"Damn mosquitoes! What the hell are these people doing? Why are they moving so slowly? Have they not eaten?!"
Han Xian, one of the leaders of the White Wave Yellow Turban Rebellion, had been dispatched here by their leader, Guo Tai, to intercept the families of Dong Zhuo’s generals.

Dong Zhuo had taken control of Bingzhou, effectively becoming the governor of the province. However, he wasn’t currently a governor, but rather the General of the Central Army of Bingzhou, responsible for controlling the province’s troops and defending against external enemies.
Dong Zhuo immediately occupied Jinyang, recruiting soldiers and constantly requesting men from Xiliang.
Jinyang was the most prosperous city in Bingzhou, originally Ding Yuan’s territory. Dong Zhuo had usurped it and driven him out, which already made Ding Yuan very unhappy.
Dispatched to Yanmen Commandery to counter Zhang Chun’s attack with the Wuhuan cavalry, he thus lured the Black Mountain Army into a chaotic battle with Dong Zhuo.
The White Wave Yellow Turbans and the Black Mountain Yellow Turbans were connected. Dong Zhuo, as a general and a member of the Xiliang elite, was difficult for others to deal with.

In fact, he repeatedly thwarted the Black Mountain Army’s attacks, forcing Zhang Yan to join forces with the White Wave Yellow Turbans to create trouble for Dong Zhuo. This led to the scene of robbing the families of generals.
For the Yellow Turbans, methods were neither honorable nor treacherous; as long as their goals were achieved, they were effective.
Regardless of the method, as long as Dong Zhuo was hampered, it was a good thing.
Like the mantis stalking the cicada, unaware of the oriole behind, Han Xian never expected to be targeted.
Leading nearly two thousand men in ambush, enduring mosquito bites, he occasionally made a slight disturbance.

If this were a military campaign, he would have been discovered long ago. He himself couldn’t bear it any longer. The deep mountains and forests, teeming with poisonous insects and snakes, made hiding in the mountains extremely dangerous.
As the carriage caravan slowly entered the encirclement, Zhang Ping’s anxiety grew.
He sensed something was wrong, but couldn’t quite pinpoint what it was. Besides, it was getting late; if they didn’t get through quickly, they’d likely have to spend the night in the wilderness.
So he shouted, "Speed up!"
Thump, thump, thump, the horses’ hooves clattered on the gravel. Halfway through, the carriage suddenly broke down and became stuck.
"What happened?" Zhang Ping asked hurriedly, startled by the horses’ neighing.
"Sir, the carriage wheels broke. We can’t move now," a guard reported after assessing the situation, awaiting Zhang Ping’s decision.
As if things weren’t going well, Zhang Ping, sensing a series of misfortunes, was about to have his wife dismount and ride away when a shout of battle erupted.
Flags appeared on the mountain, seemingly belonging to the Yellow Turbans!
"Damn it! Form ranks and meet the enemy!"
Zhang Ping roared, drawing his sword and deflecting an arrow—a skill he wasn’t lacking!
However, his guards on either side were struck by stray arrows and collapsed to the ground.
The guard force was already less than a hundred men; after this volley, many were dead. This was only because the enemy was trying to capture them alive; otherwise, very few would have survived.
"Charge! Charge! Kill all the men, leave the women!" Han Xian shouted with a lewd grin. Women?
Women were for sexual gratification!
Although as a tribal leader, he wasn’t lacking in women, how could those common beauties compare to these noblewomen of high status!
The thought of being raped by those he considered inferior filled him with shame and rage; would those noblewomen die of shame?
The sounds of hacking and slashing, the clash of weapons, pleas for mercy, and curses filled the air, even more pleas for life.
But none of it mattered. For the Yellow Turban soldiers, driven nearly mad by mosquito bites, what they needed most now was catharsis!
Killing was always the best form of release; watching blood splatter and the enemy scream was an ultimate pleasure!
Soon, only Zhang Ping remained, covered in blood, his eyes fixed intently ahead. The Yellow Turban soldiers surrounding him were of mixed clothing, some even carrying wooden spears.
"Who are you people?!"

At that moment, a man with a full beard, wearing tattered armor, emerged from the parted crowd. He carried a pair of flail hammers on his shoulders, his expression ferocious. Even before he got close, a strong stench emanated from him—a mixture of sweat and body odor!
"Whose family members are here?"
"What family members! You’ve got the wrong people! We—ah!" Before Zhang Ping could finish speaking, Han Xian brought his hammer down hard, completely crushing his foot.
"Heh!" Han Xian spat a mouthful of phlegm directly into Zhang Ping’s face, his expression extremely arrogant. "If you won’t tell me, I’ll see for myself!"
He then reached out and ripped down the carriage curtain, revealing two maids and a stunningly beautiful woman.
That mature woman, with her icy expression yet exuding an alluring aura, left him speechless. He only knew that he wanted to pin her down and take her right there and then!
"Get down!" Just as Han Xian was about to pull Madam Zou down, a commotion arose from the outer perimeter.
A warhorse charged in from another direction, followed by a group of valiant infantry.
The newcomer wore a purple-gold crown, a red-tasseled spear, and rode a magnificent steed in gleaming armor!
With a single charge, he sent the outer soldiers flying, cutting through the crowd like butter, showing no regard for anyone!

"Insignificant ants! Get out of my way! Don’t block my path! Die!" Lu Ming excitedly swung his spear like a club, each Yellow Turban soldier sent flying coughing up blood, their chests caved in. A closer look revealed bones embedded in their flesh. Even if they didn’t die, they were essentially crippled and awaiting death; there was no hope. The bones would travel through the bloodstream to their hearts, ultimately leading to their demise.
"Ugh!"
"Ah!"
"Don’t kill me!"
Thud!
Thud!

The sound of flesh being pierced was chilling, but Lu Ming showed no mercy. Instead, he grinned maliciously and continued charging forward, killing the bandits who blocked his path one by one. His methods were incredibly cruel, all to intimidate the enemy!

Besides, it was getting late; if they didn’t get through quickly, they’d likely have to spend the night in the wilderness.
So he shouted, "Speed up!"
Thump, thump, thump, the horses’ hooves clattered on the gravel.
Halfway through, the carriage suddenly broke down and became stuck.
"What happened?" Zhang Ping asked hurriedly, startled by the horses’ neighing.
"Sir, the carriage wheels broke.
We can’t move now," a guard reported after assessing the situation, awaiting Zhang Ping’s decision.
As if things weren’t going well, Zhang Ping, sensing a series of misfortunes, was about to have his wife dismount and ride away when a shout of battle erupted.
Flags appeared on the mountain, seemingly belonging to the Yellow Turbans!
"Damn it!
Form ranks and meet the enemy!"
Zhang Ping roared, drawing his sword and deflecting an arrow—a skill he wasn’t lacking!
However, his guards on either side were struck by stray arrows and collapsed to the ground.
The guard force was already less than a hundred men; after this volley, many were dead.
This was only because the enemy was trying to capture them alive; otherwise, very few would have survived.
"Charge!
Charge!
Kill all the men, leave the women!" Han Xian shouted with a lewd grin.
Women?
Women were for sexual gratification!
Although as a tribal leader, he wasn’t lacking in women, how could those common beauties compare to these noblewomen of high status!
The thought of being raped by those he considered inferior filled him with shame and rage; would those noblewomen die of shame?
The sounds of hacking and slashing, the clash of weapons, pleas for mercy, and curses filled the air, even more pleas for life.
But none of it mattered.
For the Yellow Turban soldiers, driven nearly mad by mosquito bites, what they needed most now was catharsis!
Killing was always the best form of release; watching blood splatter and the enemy scream was an ultimate pleasure!
Soon, only Zhang Ping remained, covered in blood, his eyes fixed intently ahead.
The Yellow Turban soldiers surrounding him were of mixed clothing, some even carrying wooden spears.
"Who are you people?!"
At that moment, a man with a full beard, wearing tattered armor, emerged from the parted crowd.
He carried a pair of flail hammers on his shoulders, his expression ferocious.
Even before he got close, a strong stench emanated from him—a mixture of sweat and body odor!
"Whose family members are here?"
"What family members!
You’ve got the wrong people!
We—ah!" Before Zhang Ping could finish speaking, Han Xian brought his hammer down hard, completely crushing his foot.
"Heh!" Han Xian spat a mouthful of phlegm directly into Zhang Ping’s face, his expression extremely arrogant.
"If you won’t tell me, I’ll see for myself!"
He then reached out and ripped down the carriage curtain, revealing two maids and a stunningly beautiful woman.
That mature woman, with her icy expression yet exuding an alluring aura, left him speechless.
He only knew that he wanted to pin her down and take her right there and then!
"Get down!" Just as Han Xian was about to pull Madam Zou down, a commotion arose from the outer perimeter.
A warhorse charged in from another direction, followed by a group of valiant infantry.
The newcomer wore a purple-gold crown, a red-tasseled spear, and rode a magnificent steed in gleaming armor!
With a single charge, he sent the outer soldiers flying, cutting through the crowd like butter, showing no regard for anyone!
"Insignificant ants!
Get out of my way!
Don’t block my path!
Die!" Lu Ming excitedly swung his spear like a club, each Yellow Turban soldier sent flying coughing up blood, their chests caved in.
A closer look revealed bones embedded in their flesh.
Even if they didn’t die, they were essentially crippled and awaiting death; there was no hope.
The bones would travel through the bloodstream to their hearts, ultimately leading to their demise.
"Ugh!"
"Ah!"
"Don’t kill me!"
Thud!
Thud!
The sound of flesh being pierced was chilling, but Lu Ming showed no mercy.
Instead, he grinned maliciously and continued charging forward, killing the bandits who blocked his path one by one.
His methods were incredibly cruel, all to intimidate the enemy!

chapters.title: Chapter 181 Remember not to swear.
paragraphs: The timing was perfect. Too early, and the Yellow Turban army might be scared away; too late, and Lady Zou might suffer a terrible fate.
It was about striking the right rhythm, arriving at the perfect time.
The perfect pace—not too slow, not too fast—to get there in time, rescue Lady Zou, and leave her no time to explain. He could take her back and rape her first!

Once they were comfortable with each other, even if Zhang Ji saw it, he could claim Lady Zou had been kidnapped by the Yellow Turbans, and he had rescued her while attacking the Yellow Turban rebels in Anyi City, taking her as a concubine because of her beauty.
Then, even Zhang Ji would have no grounds for complaint; it wasn’t like he had forcibly taken her.
Even if he was angry, it wouldn’t be towards him. He couldn’t protect his wife; she had been taken from him. Who could he blame?
The long-dormant desire could finally be released. Just thinking about it made Lu Ming incredibly excited.
This was exactly the feeling he wanted, this was exactly the effect he wanted.
He hadn’t been with a woman for days; enduring this long was a testament to his strong will.

At this moment, the system’s intelligence told him that a beautiful married woman, even Cao Cao would be captivated by, was passing by, and he could satisfy his lust. Not acting now would be a disservice to himself and his manhood.
Han Xian was initially stunned by Madam Zou’s beauty, but the shouts of battle ahead prevented him from immediately regaining his composure.
It was entirely because a beautiful and elegant mature woman was before him, distracting him and diverting his attention!
By the time he reacted, Lu Ming had already charged into the center, unmatched in combat. All his men seemed like wooden statues before him!
If he had faced a coordinated battle formation, with shields to block, spear thrusts, and archer attacks, Lu Ming certainly wouldn’t have broken through so easily.

The key issue was the Yellow Turbans’ poor equipment. Most were swept in during the initial invasion, their weapons limited to wooden spears. This illustrates the extent of their lack of resources; they lacked even iron weapons—their equipment was rudimentary to the extreme!
Such a rebel army was destined to have low morale. They might be effective in a favorable situation, but in a disadvantageous battle, they were simply a joke.

Lu Ming, however, saw through this. He led the charge, using overwhelming pressure to force the Yellow Turban soldiers to their breaking point. When fear reached its peak, their legs went weak, and they couldn’t even move!
Xiang Yu was able to break through the encirclement of tens of thousands of troops with only twenty-eight knights by exploiting this momentum and the weaknesses of their formation.
Now, Lu Ming was replicating this, but with only minor difficulty.
His personal guards began to coordinate their attacks, with swordsmen and shield-wielding infantrymen in front, blocking attacks while simultaneously counterattacking.
The halberd-wielding soldiers used long halberds, similar to spears, but with hooked tips. Skilled users could even use them to pull away enemy weapons.
Archers, on the other hand, drew their bows, aimed, and fired a single shot to the throat, leaving no chance for the enemy to recover.
A hit to the face, throat, or heart—weak points—was often an instant kill.
Even if the arrow hit other areas, a follow-up shot from a soldier in front could finish the job.
Killing enemies earned experience.
Soldiers also needed experience to level up. While the specific rules for transporting them were unknown, killing usually yielded the most experience.
Slash wounds were also possible, but less common.
Only by fighting and participating in battles could one gain experience.
These second-tier troops, while not exactly like tigers among sheep, demonstrated overwhelming superiority against the Yellow Turban rebels.
Four or five hundred Yellow Turban soldiers stood in the way, utterly powerless to resist. Even those who charged forward, howling, were quickly cut down.
The well-organized attack formation of the imperial guards resembled a meat grinder; anyone who went in would die!
Faced with this situation, a sense of fear began to spread.
When the death toll exceeded four hundred, someone shouted, and everyone fled in terror, too afraid to confront the government troops.
Even Lu Ming, who had charged in, was unharmed, showing no fear whatsoever, treating these ambushing bandits as mere toys for his amusement!

"Don’t run! Anyone who dares to run! Grab your weapons and charge! They’re so few, what are they afraid of! Why run!" Faced with the formidable enemy, Han Xian finally turned his attention back, stunned by the sight of the government soldiers relentlessly cutting down the grass.
He had fought his entire life, following the Yellow Turban Rebellion from the time of Zhang Jiao’s uprising, experiencing countless battles large and small, including one against the Xiongnu.
But he had never seen soldiers with such fighting prowess, completely different from the soldiers who had previously besieged them!
Especially the commander at the front, he was practically a demon, utterly terrifying!
How could such a terrifying person exist?!
Thud! Thud!
Ah! Ah!
Even with Han Xian relentlessly cutting down fleeing soldiers, the rout was becoming increasingly difficult to stop. Once the rout began, turning the tide was virtually impossible.

In just a few minutes, Lu Ming burst in front of Han Xian, mounted on his warhorse, looking down at the Yellow Turban leader reeking of body odor. The two characters "Han Xian" were etched on his forehead; it was impossible not to recognize him!

He only glanced at her briefly, catching only a glimpse of Zou’s profile. Her long, dark hair clung to her face, her features were dignified and beautiful, and her clothes were neat and tidy; she didn’t appear to have been insulted.
Even just her profile exuded a captivating and alluring charm!
Her hands were as white as jade, and her neck, like that of a swan, was exquisitely slender. It was unimaginable what kind of spiritual essence could have nurtured such a beauty!

However, being a man who had been with many women, withstood the pressure from the Yuan family, and had even been deceived by the current emperor, Lu Ming was only slightly shocked before recovering. He pointed his gun at Han Xian, "You’re a man of your stature, I’ll spare your life. Heh, you’re quite something, but how much? Tell Yang Feng for me that I thank him!"

"Don’t be so arrogant! Spare my life! Bah! You’re the one who should die! You little bastard! When I was out traveling the country, you were probably still playing in the mud! *Splat!*" Han Xian had barely finished speaking when his throat was pierced, his eyes fixed on Lu Ming, a look of unresolved resentment in his eyes as he died!

chapters.title: Chapter 182 Snatched Madam Zou
paragraphs: Lu Ming despised people who spewed filth. He could insult and humiliate others, but no one could treat him like that!
Because he had a system; he was a tyrant, able to rise to power unexpectedly, while others were merely mortals. He, however, was a tyrant with a lifespan of three hundred years!
How dare he call him a bastard? He was tired of living!
He had originally intended to spare Han Xian’s life to incite internal strife within the Yellow Turban Army; otherwise, he wouldn’t have mentioned the name of another leader, Yang Feng. What a pity.
Han Xian’s filth was intolerable, so he had to endure it!
With a swift backhand, he severed Han Xian’s head, wrapped it in a rag, and placed it on the horse. Turning to Madam Zou, he frowned. "Can you ride a horse?"
"No." A hint of fear flashed in Madam Zou’s eyes. For a moment, she couldn’t tell if Lu Ming was a good person or a bad person. Judging from his appearance, he seemed like a good person.

"Hmph! What a nuisance." Lu Ming swiftly killed the bandit who tried to ambush him, then plunged back into the crowd, slaughtering his way through. He didn’t go far, focusing his killing spree around the carriage where Madam Zou was.
His personal guards caught up, driving the fleeing bandits away.
Some were wounded, some even with their limbs severed and immobilized.
Lu Ming first cast the spell ’Diamond Body Protection,’ clearing away the negative emotions of bleeding and fear.
Then he bandaged the seriously wounded, simply setting and stabilizing fractures, quickly suturing wounds, and applying herbal dressings.
The whole process took less than three minutes, emphasizing speed.
Madam Zou observed Lu Ming, mentally considering how to declare her identity. If she could rely on him to successfully return to her husband, Zhang Ji, it wouldn’t be a bad thing.
However, she couldn’t help but worry that he might be tempted by her beauty!
In the past, Zhang Ji had kept Madam Zou confined at home, preventing her from showing her face in public, not out of love, but out of possessiveness.

Knowing that Madam Zou easily attracted the covetousness of men, and also to guard against Dong Zhuo, a lecherous man who had slept with many of his concubines, he naturally couldn’t let Dong Zhuo know. Therefore, Madam Zou was rarely seen by anyone. A beauty capable of bringing ruin to the country couldn’t be protected without equal strength; ultimately, she became a source of trouble, not a confidante!
After his personal guards surrounded him, Lu Ming no longer needed to kill indiscriminately.
Healing could also provide experience; for him, killing was merely to set an example.
If he had reliable generals under his command, he wouldn’t need to do everything personally; this situation was truly unavoidable.
Stopping down beside the carriage, Lu Ming took out some wood and began to repair it.

The carriage wheel was broken; a new one could be made on the spot and installed. It wasn’t a difficult task; he even managed to hold up the carriage with one hand and change the wheel with the other, despite having three women inside. This kind of strength was truly astonishing. No man could possibly do that; it was unbelievable!
The carriage was repaired in just twenty minutes. When he looked up again, the Yellow Turban rebels had vanished without a trace.
Han Xian’s death, combined with his charge, had nearly wiped them out.
These rebels, who could only fight with the wind at their backs, had escaped, and would likely spread panic, which perfectly suited his next move.
He ordered his personal guards to drive the carriage, collected all the weapons and armor, stripped them naked, piled the bodies together, added firewood, and burned them.
Without even looking back, Lu Ming and his men left.
The flames flickered in the mountains, thick smoke billowing, visible even from several hilltops away.
Only a few crows circling in the sky cawed strangely, seemingly dissatisfied with the lack of food.
The journey there took an hour, but the return trip took an extra half hour.
Because of the carriage, some sections were difficult to traverse, forcing them to take detours.
The bumpy carriage ride nearly made Madam Zou vomit. She suppressed her nausea, and her two personal maids were also pale, clearly suffering from the same discomfort.
But being dependent on others, and unsure of their fate, they too were suppressing their urge to vomit.
They hurriedly went out and quietly returned.
They didn’t even disturb anyone, simply bringing the carriage in.
Jiang Qin did see Madam Zou and the others get out of the carriage and enter the commander’s tent, but this was none of his concern.
Lu Ming was the lord and the commander; it was perfectly normal for him to indulge in women.
The rule in the army was that women were forbidden. Most of the time, the soldiers were men driven by lust, needing an outlet for their pent-up desires after brutal battles.
They either gambled or sought out women.
Generally, after conquering a city, most armies would indulge in debauchery for several days, naturally involving the rape of women.
The unfortunate ones were the ordinary civilians, or small, powerful families.
The presence of women in the military camp easily led to mutiny.
This rule was strictly enforced, but sometimes rules were meant to be broken.
This rule had no binding force on the commander-in-chief.

To cite a recent example, Cao Cao’s cousin, Cao Hong, was a man who knew how to enjoy life. Even on campaigns, he liked to bring singing girls with him, drinking and dancing, indulging in a great deal of pleasure.
Lu Ming’s main tent was large and featured a layered, framed design, making it easy to fold.

The inner layer contained charcoal, while the outer layer was sewn with waterproof fabric. It was rainproof, sound-absorbing, and air-filtering, and its weight wasn’t too heavy—a perfect and highly practical solution.
After arranging for Madam Zou to sit in an inner cubicle, Lu Ming pointed to the bathtub and said, "Wash yourselves clean, then lie down on the bed and wait for my favor."
"My lord," Madam Zou tried to explain her identity, but Lu Ming glared at her, and she swallowed her words.
She was just a weak woman, without power, without equal standing to negotiate with Lu Ming—she had no right whatsoever.
What could she do now?
Being humiliated was a foregone conclusion. Although she didn’t want to admit it, this was the bloody reality; she was about to lose her chastity.
She was about to betray her husband, opening her legs to welcome a man who didn’t belong to her husband!

chapters.title: Chapter 183 Zhang Ji’s Guide to Green Hats
paragraphs: Zhang Jizheng, who was far away in Jinyang, was preparing to set off to Yanmen County to stop the rebels’ attack.
He always felt a little restless and at a loss today. He didn’t know why, but he always felt that something was about to happen.

He felt that there might be dangers on the battlefield. Many times, military commanders who have been on the battlefield for a long time will have such an intuition, an intuition that can judge what the situation will be like.
He has a unique set of judgments about danger. Now it seems that he needs to be more careful.
"Uncle, is something wrong?" asked a young man with resolute eyes next to him. This man had a resolute face and was approaching his thirties, which was the prime time for him to be strong.
Zhang Xiu!
A ruthless man who could make Cao Cao lose his army and his son!
A ruthless man who killed Cao Cao’s son and died a good death!
The spear king of the North, Zhang Xiu!
Zhang Xiu has a good reputation, but among so many powerful generals in Xiliang, he is not outstanding.
Hua Xiong is no worse than him. He is even better at leading troops in battles.
Therefore, even if he is good at martial arts and can lead troops into battle, up to now he has only held the position of chief clerk, which is far behind Lu Ming!

A middle-aged man in tattered armor listened to his teacher’s report in a letter, his face ashen with disbelief.

"Abandon Anze City and launch a preemptive attack? This is absurd! We don’t even know who killed Brother Han Xian, and instead of avenging him, you want us to launch a preemptive attack? Unthinkable!"
Hu Cai slammed his fist on the table. He had already received the news.
His younger brother, Hu Long, had been killed in Anyi City, murdered by the Jin family.
He was now consumed by thoughts of avenging his brother and had no interest in Guo Tai’s affairs.
The Yellow Turban Army was riddled with factions. Although Guo Tai was a leader, he had only risen to that position because he commanded a large army.
The other leaders also had their own forces, and they only united because of the rebellion; otherwise, they wouldn’t have obeyed anyone else’s orders.
Things are different now. Back then, they had Zhang Jiao, the great and wise teacher, to keep them in check, and they could still unite as one. Now, they’re nothing but bandits in yellow turbans.

"Hu Cai, don’t be angry. The court has sent people to quell the rebellion, and it’s right to deal with the court’s troops first. Look at Zhang Yan, he succeeded! The court couldn’t wipe him out, and they even promoted him. Hmph, if we can thwart the court’s encirclement this time, we can also get some official positions!" If we go and take Anyi City, and capture those officers, wouldn’t we be able to sell them for a good price?"
Using hostages to exchange for fame and fortune? This seems somewhat naive, but it also carries some risks.
Yang Feng stared at the rudimentary map, pondering the feasibility of his plan.
He knew that the Yellow Turban rebels had never won a single battle against a large government army.
They were either outnumbered or utterly crushed. He knew his own strength. "It’s possible," he said, "but Anyi City is heavily fortified; it won’t be easy to take."

With you and me, brothers, controlling a city and so many men under our command, we won’t have to worry about the court going back on its word!"
